comments.author: story-repo
comments.body:
**Addition: paper-repo asks you to confirm or correct its identification of 2610.02344's escape condition (relayed from story-repo#11).** The manuscript already states it: paper-repo 9cd4c88, Sec. 1, Sec. 2 and the appendix paragraph "The stability count of De Melo Costa et al.". paper-repo changes those three passages if your reading disagrees. Their derivation, from the v1 PDF, App. J.1 (p. 48):

- **Their notation.** γ_kℓ = c_k q_ℓ and σ_kℓ = a_k p_ℓ, where:
  - a_k and c_k are the eigenvalues of Σ11 and Σ_X1 along data mode k;
  - p_ℓ and q_ℓ are the eigenvalues of P = W_pᵀW_p and Q = W_pᵀM̄_2 along predictor mode ℓ.
- **Encoder decay.** Prop. J.1 makes it an additive floor: (k, ℓ) escapes iff γ_kℓ − σ_kℓ > η_wd. The decay acts on the context encoder only.
- **The delivered aligned model.** Take a scalar predictor gain p0, no target mask (M̄_2 = I) and a stop-gradient or EMA target. Then q = p0, p_ℓ = p0², a_k = σ_k and c_k = c_k. The condition becomes p0 c_k − p0² σ_k − λ_W > 0, i.e. g_k(p0) > 0: the **initial window**.
- **EMA.** Their J.7 says the EMA rate changes the speed of escape, not which modes escape. This matches the delivered result that the EMA root has the sign of g_k at fixed gain.
- **Where the identification is not immediate:**
  - random Gaussian predictors and non-commuting statistics, where their criterion counts (k, ℓ) pairs under spectral decoupling;
  - masked targets (M̄_2 ≠ I, E2);
  - deep predictors.

**Measured since (experiment-repo, for your check):**
- 112f91e: their signed form (App. C.8) agrees with the initial window run by run in every aligned and circulant arm.
- 409a766 adds their paired Eq. 51/Eq. 7 predictor side and the exact linearisation:
  - random-predictor arm: best variant MAE 3.02, against the race's 0.69;
  - non-commuting arm, exact form: 1.28, against 0.11;
  - their count exceeds measured rank, although it is stated as a bound, in 57% of aligned E1b runs and 26% of E2 cyclic runs.

**What I need from you on this point:** confirm the identification, or state where it fails, with their section and equation numbers. The same answer settles P1 of the plan. Your brief fc92d92 Sec. 5.1 already reads it the same way; an explicit confirmation here closes the loop for paper-repo and for internal-review-repo's E5 verdict.

comments.author: idea-repo
comments.body:
**Answer to #4, all items plus both additions. Pushed as brief v4.2, idea-repo 5f0fe3335b800d3ffd6b70d25b355f2e16ad667d.** Item 1 is now `brief.md` §5.1; items 2–4 are §5.3. The underlying notes are `refs/lit_dvd2610.md` (2610.02344 and its code at 3176215b; §9.4 corrected) and `refs/lit_directions_ABC.md` (new). 103 new bib entries are merged into `refs/refs.bib`, all arXiv v1 ≤ 2026-10-17.

### Addition 2: paper-repo's identification is confirmed, with three qualifications
For a scalar predictor, Prop. J.1 (App. J.1, p. 48), with γ_kℓ = c_k q_ℓ and σ_kℓ = a_k p_ℓ (Eq. 7 / Cor. A.4), gives **exactly the delivered initial window g_k(p0) > 0**. Its count is the window count, not the static bound c_k²/(4σ_k) > λ_W, and not anything time-dependent. paper-repo's three passages at 9cd4c88 can stand. Prop. J.7 is the EMA statement; their Eq. 28 is our EMA root equation at λ_W = 0. Qualifications to state in the text:

1. **The headline criterion has no weight decay.** Eq. 6/7 count {μ > 1}, i.e. #{k : p0 < c_k/σ_k}. That is the window's upper edge only, with no lower edge. Report it as a second variant next to J.1. If App. C.8 "signed form" (112f91e) already includes η_wd, it is the J.1 variant. Please check which one 112f91e scored.

2. **Masked targets (E2) and input-space masking are a transfer, not their literal model.** Their target is the full input, encoded and then masked in feature space (M̄_2, so q = p0·p_tgt). Their context is masked in input space (Σ_X1 = p_m1 Σ_XX, Eq. 38; Lemma 3.1 needs M_2 independent of x). The linearised structure is the same, though: drive = cross-covariance ⊗ W_pᵀ(·), decay = context covariance ⊗ W_pᵀW_p, with η_wd additive. So substituting our masked moments σ_k, c_k (eq. bernoulli) is the natural reading. Phrase it as "their criterion applied with our masked moments". For cyclic masks the Fourier basis satisfies their Ass. 3.2 exactly.

3. **Random or non-commuting predictors.**
   - Eq. 7 and the pairing (k, ℓ) need Ass. 3.2 (shared orthonormal eigenbases, real spectra).
   - Without it, their exact object is the number of unstable eigenvalues of J at the origin: Thm A.1, det Q(λ) with Q(λ) = λ²I + λ(S + βI) + β(S − G). Here S = Σ_c ⊗ P0ᵀP0 + λ_W I and G = Σ_tcᵀ ⊗ P0ᵀM̄.
   - r_tight (Eq. 8) bounds that count. They state it as an upper bound on rank W_+(t) **of the linearised flow** (Cor. 3.3), not on the final rank.
   - So 409a766's "exact linearisation" is the right head-to-head. The 57% / 26% bound violations are expected, because with predictor decay the modes that escape early can die later: the race's point. Say that rather than calling their bound "wrong".

   **Deep predictors.** Near the collapsed point the encoder gradient depends only on the end-to-end predictor map, and every predictor layer's gradient is quadratic in W (their Lemma 3.4 / F.2 argument). The identification therefore holds with P0 = product of the predictor factors (E1c: p0 = end-to-end gain).

### Item 1: 2610.02344 at equation level (details in brief §5.1)
- **Regime.** They linearise at W = W_a = 0 with W_p at its O(1) value, so the predictor is order one and not collapsed. It is quasi-static near collapse (Lemma 3.4, Thm F.3).
  - Predictor weight decay never appears.
  - Encoder weight decay appears only in J.1, where "the decay acts on the context encoder only". The headline Eq. 6 omits it.
- **μ computable from a run's inputs alone.** In our notation, with σ_k, c_k the masked moments and P0 the initial predictor:
  - scalar P0 = p0 I: r_μ = #{k : p0 < c_k/σ_k}; r_J1 = #{k : g_k(p0) > 0}.
  - commuting matrix P0: U = {(k, ℓ) : c_k q_ℓ/(σ_k p_ℓ) > 1}, or γ − σ > λ_W with weight decay, using q_ℓ = eig(P0ᵀM̄) and p_ℓ = eig(P0ᵀP0). Then r_tight = min(|π_k U|, |π_ℓ U|, d, N). The experiments use the absolute-value form (Eqs. 51–52).
  - general: the unstable-eigenvalue count of Thm A.1 above.
  - λ_P does not enter. The EMA rate does not change membership.
- **Already scored by the delivered baselines.** The `rank_window` in `code/e1b.py` and `code/e2.py` is the J.1 count on aligned runs.
  - E1b: window 3.7 vs race 0.25 (static 11.2).
  - E2 cyclic: window 1.04 vs race 0.03 (static 4.04).
  - **Not** scored in the delivered code: the headline variant; randpred (no window was computed there); noncomm (the delivered window pairs sorted eigenvalues, an approximation). 409a766 now covers the last two.
- **Directions it treats.** AdamW: no, it is gradient flow only. Normalised targets: no; isotropy/variance penalties appear only as negative decay (J.3, J.4). Schedules: EMA as a timescale only, no weight-decay schedule. Post-capture: only the adiabatic Thm F.1 (τ_crit). Deep or nonlinear: no theory; images are handled "by analogy" (§7). Timing: init-only by construction; they concede that on images the mediating variable is "measured after predictor equilibration, not at initialisation" (§6.2, K.1).
- **Precedent to cite.** Prop. J.5 (mimetic init) uses an integrated growth ∫λ⁺dt > log 10³ along a decaying identity dose at fixed Frobenius norm. It is the nearest thing to the race, but it is not gain decay and not a rank predictor.
- **ResidualPred** (brief §5.1 corrects v4.1, which wrongly said the benefit "must come from the race"):
  - *Image* (`image/src/models/vision_transformer.py`, `ResidualPredPredictor`): a learnable per-head diag_bias·I, initialised at β = 10, added to the context–context attention block only. MLP fc2 is zero-initialised and not decayed. predictor_embed/proj use trunc-normal std 0.02, with a final LayerNorm before proj.
  - So the image ResidualPred's end-to-end gain is **not 1**; K.1 measures ≈ 0.31 for both blocks. Its identity is a token-routing prior (their App. E.3), outside both linear theories.
  - *Tabular*: z + ΔW z with ΔW ~ N(0, init_scale²), so p0 ≈ 1.
  - In the delivered theory a scalar p0 above p_+ makes directions shrink first, which lowers rank. So no gain-based ResidualPred benefit is predicted by either theory.
  - Numbers: linear probe +4.1 / +4.0 / +4.1 / +5.6 pp (CIFAR-10/100, STL-10, IN-100); IN-1k pilot 31.69 vs 25.22. Frozen at init it collapses (I.8).
  - Any predictor-design claim must be compared with it or the paper must say why not.
- **Tabular-JEPA, for P3.**
  - Data: OpenML aloi 1592, helena 41169, jannis 41168; min-max scaled, 80/10/10 split.
  - Model: linear encoder, Kaiming scale 1 (**not near collapse at init**); embed 64; batch 256; 30 epochs; AdamW lr 1e-3 cosine, wd 1e-5; EMA 0.996→1.
  - Grid `critical_2d` (`tabular/experiment_1.py`): predictor std {1e-4 … 10} × context {0.001 … 0.8} × 3 seeds × 3 datasets = 810 runs.
  - Rank: entropy effective rank (`collapse_metrics.py::compute_effective_rank`).
  - μ: `JacobianAnalyzer`, at epoch 0 and the last epoch. Columns are in `results/tabular_phase_grid/grid_<ds>.csv`; per-run values incl. `rc_r_tight_abs` are in `full_sweep_per_run.csv`.
  - Entry point: `cd tabular && bash reproduce_tabular.sh --linear-only --dataset <ds>`.
  - **Their per-step decoupled decay lr·wd ≤ 1e-8 makes λ_P ≈ 0, where the race reduces to the window.** On the published grid the two criteria should agree. Discriminating cells need wd ≈ 1e-3…1e-1, and a small encoder init if the near-collapse regime is wanted.
  - Their T-JEPA Tab. 16 (jannis) is already a μ > 1 failure: α = 0.01 has μ_50 = 1.11–4.22 and collapses in 4/5 contexts, while α = 0.05 has μ_50 < 1 and learns 6/6. That is two-sided, as a window or lost race predicts.

### Addition 1: status and novelty
- 2610.02344 is **prior work accepted at NeurIPS 2026**. Brief §5.1 now says so; bib key `demelocosta2026drive`.
- **Credit to them:**
  - the drive-vs-decay framing;
  - linearisation at the collapsed point with an O(1) predictor;
  - the per-mode ratio and its factorisation;
  - heuristics as doses on μ: scale, masking, EMA (speed only), encoder weight decay;
  - EMA not changing membership;
  - the frozen identity predictor collapsing (J.6, I.8);
  - "large encoder weight decay stabilises collapse" (J.1). **This is not novel on its own.**
- **Distinct:**
  - predictor weight decay and the decaying gain p(t);
  - collapse as the eventual attractor once p → 0, and the necessity of predictor decay for any survivor (Prop. fixed (c));
  - the race/capture separatrix, with λ^race far below the static threshold and rank non-monotone in λ and p0;
  - pre-registered tests where their criterion (= initial window) is measured worse;
  - the masking statistics with input-space context and target masks.

### Item 2: Direction A (Adam/AdamW, normalised targets)
- **No SSL/JEPA collapse analysis under Adam/AdamW exists.** An AdamW race is new.
- Closest results:
  - `sabanayagam2026optimizer` (2610.04249, posted 2026-10-03): under sign descent, mode birth from a small seed takes **bounded** time, because factors grow linearly; ε brings back GD-like growth at tiny gradients. No decay, no predictor.
  - `jacobs2026never` Lemma 4.5: under sign flow with decoupled decay, |w_i| − |w_j| is damped by e^{−∫α}. That gives the AdamW analogue of the balance identity, |p| − |a| = e^{−ηλt}(|p0| − |a0|) (our inference).
  - `kunstner2024heavy` Thm 3: sign descent removes the dependence of rate on signal strength. Our predicted consequence: AdamW is **less spectrally selective**, with more survivors at equal decay. That fits the delivered AdamW numbers (static 5.1 vs race 13.7) and is testable.
  - `tang2025understanding`: Adam with coupled L2 gets stuck at small init above an init-dependent λ; AdamW does not.
  - `wang2024set`: decoupled decay gives a 1/(ηλ) memory, the natural clock for AdamW.
  - `xie2024implicit`: if AdamW converges, it does so inside the ℓ∞ box ‖x‖∞ ≤ 1/λ.
  - `zhao2026optimizer`: sign descent can push a GD-collapsed direction to O(1/λ). In linear JEPA the gradient is exactly 0 on the collapsed set, so this acts only through coupling.
  - Caveat: Adam is not rotation invariant (`xie2024adam`).
- **Normalised targets.**
  - I-JEPA LayerNorms the target twice (`F.layer_norm` after the encoder's own affine LN, `src/train.py` l. 298). 1-D parameters are not decayed.
  - So in the ViT only dimensional collapse is possible, and only non-normalised projections such as `predictor_proj` carry a gain that weight decay shrinks.
  - Empirically: `colton2025elucidating` (I-JEPA target-LN study, no collapse analysis); `lowe2026self` (z-scored targets still collapse in rank after about 200 epochs).
  - The only dynamics theory is still Bao 2023 (gradient flow).
  - Open: the race restated on the sphere.

### Item 3: Direction B (after the first escape, schedules, noise)
- **Staircase without decay:** Berthier; Pesme-Flammarion 2023; Jin 2023; Zhang-Saxe-Latham 2025; ViT rank steps (Boix-Adsera 2023).
- **Integrated-utility-vs-log(1/init) activation, losers carrying their norms:** AGF (`kunin2025alternating`). This is the closest race-like rule, but it has no decay and no deadline. Cite and distinguish.
- **SGD noise:**
  - collapsed directions are invariant, and attractive when L'' + D''/2 > 0 (`chen2023stochastic`, checked). This gives a window g_k − D_k/2;
  - noise acts as extra decay and a smaller effective init (Pillaud-Vivien 2022; Pesme 2021). **It never reseeds**;
  - only additive reseeding or symmetry breaking revives directions: syre, with SimCLR low-rankness 70% → 0% (`ziyin2024remove`); shrink-and-perturb; continual backprop; L2 Init.
- **Schedules:**
  - the only weight-decay-schedule ablation is DINO's 0.04→0.4 ramp, 78.0 vs ≤ 76.9 fixed (`morningstar2024augmentations`). It reports accuracy only;
  - rank vs weight-decay/EMA schedules is **measured nowhere**, including LiDAR's late RankMe decline;
  - `lewkowycz2020training`: a kernel shrunk by weight decay closes a window at t ~ 1/λ.

### Item 4: Direction C (deep/ReLU, timing, λ-JEPA)
- **Balance identity.** p² − a² = e^{−2λt}(p0² − a0²) is the η → 0 case of `kunin2020neural` Eq. 20 (checked). The matrix form is `kobayashi2024weight` Lemma B.1. The delivered paper credits only Tian Thm 1. **Add these; the identity is not new, the per-direction deadline built from it is.**
- **λ-JEPA** (`demirel2026lambdajepa`, cite v1 of 2026-09-28):
  - Thm A.7 with γ = 0 is the same identity, but for a supervised two-layer net;
  - its guarantee uses the **opposite** imbalance sign (encoder-heavy Δ < 0, floor a² ≥ −Δ), while ours is predictor-heavy;
  - its log-det term makes Δ⋆ = −γ/λ a permanent floor, which removes the race. It is a fix, not a timing theory.
- **Our start is "upstream" δ > 0** (`kunin2024get`, checked): lazy in linear regression, fastest alignment in ReLU.
- **ReLU:** small-init early phases last about log(1/init) and can permanently fail to activate directions (`boursier2024early`, same init sign; `min2023early`).
- **Deeper homogeneous nets:** the early phase lasts a power of 1/init (`kumar2024early`), so deeper encoders should lose against a fixed window more easily (our inference). With more than one hidden layer the origin is a local minimum under weight decay (`ziyin2022exact`).
- **"Race" with the same conserved quantity:** `kleinman2023critical` (deep linear, pathway competition, early deficits permanent, no weight decay). **Must be cited and distinguished.**
- **Decided early:**
  - weight decay matters early (`golatkar2019time`; Achille, Frankle, Fort);
  - weight decay shrinking a large factor switches regime globally at log(scale)/λ (`lyu2023dichotomy`, checked). This is the nearest formal analogue of the deadline;
  - no SSL paper shows that rank is decided in an early, weight-decay-dependent window.

**Not established.**
- Tarmoun 2021 and Xu 2023: venues not independently verified.
- A few formulas came from sub-agent reading and are flagged in the notes: Li-Arora factor, Wan angular value, the Neural Mechanics finite-η term.
- Sabanayagam-Lucey and Tang: main-text statements only, proofs not read.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
The previous world in this line of work delivered a complete paper on representation collapse in joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs): a theory in which collapse is decided early in training, near the collapsed solution, by a competition in every direction of representation space between a driving force that grows the direction and a decay effect that shrinks it, together with experiments that test it. That paper, its code and its results are in your repositories and workspaces. Take them as the starting point, not as the work to redo.

Extend that paper with the next piece of research on this problem. Begin from what it leaves open: its stated limitations, its predictions that were not tested or did not hold, the settings its theory does not reach (for example nonlinear or deep encoders, realistic data and architectures, training far from the collapsed solution), and what the theory implies for designing or choosing the heuristics that prevent collapse. Choose the directions that most advance the understanding of when and why JEPAs collapse, and carry them through to new theoretical or empirical results.

Deliver the extended paper, ready to submit to ICLR 2027 and written to the venue's submission requirements: the LaTeX source in the ICLR 2027 template, the compiled PDF, and the code and experimental results that the paper's claims rest on. Keep what still holds from the delivered paper, revise what the new results change, and make clear what the extension adds.

Do not use any paper, preprint, code release or other written work first published after 18 October 2026.

issue.author: story-repo
issue.body:
**Need:** for the plan's comparisons and baselines (`plan.md` v0.1 in world/story-repo, sections 2, 4 and 7), three things from the prior-work map, each with a verifiable first-publication date on or before 2026-09-01:

1. **Which of the plan's candidate predictions are already established, and where.** Plan section 2 lists P1-P7 for a linear JEPA near collapse (per-direction growth rate g_k(p) = p c_k - p^2 sigma_k - lambda; survival/rank criterion; stop-gradient necessary by Cauchy-Schwarz; no-predictor fails when c_k <= sigma_k; masking sets c_k/sigma_k; EMA changes the growth rate but not the threshold; weight decay raises the threshold). For each: is it stated or implied in prior work (e.g. eigenmode analyses of BYOL/SimSiam/DirectPred with predictor, weight decay and EMA; analyses of the predictor's role; implicit variance regularisation; deep-linear JEPA implicit bias; stepwise/saddle-to-saddle SSL dynamics; dimensional collapse in contrastive SSL; explicitly regularised JEPAs such as LeJEPA if its date qualifies), and what exactly does that work show vs. not show? This decides which claims can be called new and what the paper must compare against.
2. **The standard I-JEPA recipe** and its small-scale variants: context/target block scales and number of target blocks (mask ratio), predictor depth/width/embedding dim, EMA momentum schedule, weight decay schedule, optimiser/LR, and any published small-image (CIFAR-scale, 32x32) I-JEPA or JEPA settings with collapse observations. E3 sweeps are centred on these.
3. **Conventions for the measurements:** effective rank definitions (RankMe and alternatives), how prior work reports collapse and per-direction dynamics, and the linear-probe protocol used at CIFAR scale.

**For:** the comparison section and novelty statements (claims C1-C3), the E3 baseline, and the metrics in every experiment.

**Already known:** your brief v1 (eb9f7a1) section 4 conventions; candidate references from memory only (Tian et al. 2021; Littwin et al. 2024; Halvagal et al. 2023; Assran et al. 2023 I-JEPA; Garrido et al. 2023 RankMe; Jing et al. 2022; Simon et al. 2023), none verified by me.

**Waiting on it:** plan v1 sections 4 and 7, and experiment-repo's E3 baseline settings (E1/E2 proceed without it).
issue.title: Prior work the plan must compare against: which drive/decay predictions are established, I-JEPA recipe values, measurement conventions

comments.author: idea-repo
comments.body:
The answer is pushed in idea-repo at 45cdf9242a434e589590aed6c0606804886b084c. All sources have a verified v1 date on or before 2026-09-01.

**1. Which of P1–P7 are already established.** Details are in `brief.md` §5.6 (a table: plan item → prior work → what is new). Equations are in `refs/lit_theory.md` and `refs/lit_tools.md`.

Your g_k(p) = p c_k − p²σ_k − λ maps onto prior notation as follows:
- It is exactly Tian, Chen & Ganguli's ICML 2021 Δ_j = τp − (1+s²)p² − η, with c ↔ τ and σ ↔ 1+s².
- Littwin et al. 2024's regression coefficient ρ = c/σ.
- Halvagal et al. 2023's λ_m(1−λ_m) is g at c = σ = 1, λ = 0.

Status of each prediction:
- **P1 (static threshold c²/(4σ) > λ): established in form.** Tian 2021 (all modes collapse iff η > τ²/(4(1+s²))), Wang, Chen, Du & Tian 2021 (2110.04947), and PEIRA (Arbel, Terver & Ponce, 2605.17671, 2026-05-17: c² ≥ 4λ). These cover augmentation noise with isotropic data, and a drive that is quadratic at the origin.
  - New: anisotropic c_k, σ_k from masking, and the first-order-drive regime.
  - In Tian's invariant WWᵀ = α_p⁻¹W_pᵀW_p + e^{−2ηt}C, your regime (predictor O(1) while the encoder is small) is the *unbalanced* initialisation C ≫ 0. Tian sets it aside by analysing the parabola C → 0. The paper must say this, or reviewers will treat it as Tian 2021.
- **P2: partly established.** Ordering by growth rate and stepwise rank are known: Simon et al. ICML 2023, Littwin 2024 (greedy in ρ), Saxe 2014. Tian has the basin picture under weight decay (a mode survives iff p_j > p*_−).
  - New: the race criterion computed from statistics, init scales and hyperparameters, and testing it as a rank predictor in neural JEPAs.
- **P3: established.** Tian 2021 (no stop-grad gives vec(W)' = −H vec(W) with H PSD), Halvagal 2023 (rate −(1−λ)²), Ponce et al. 2025 (2507.01028); empirically SimSiam and BYOL. Present it as a consistency check and cite these.
- **P4: partly established.**
  - The window 0 < p < c/σ is Halvagal's λ(1−λ).
  - Predictor learning rate: Tian finds a larger α_p shrinks the basin and a too-large one stops growth. BYOL App. I: without EMA the predictor lr must be ×2 or more (×1 gives 5.5%, ×2 gives 62.8%).
  - Wen & Li 2022: the predictor rescues weak features.
  - New: init scale, width and depth acting as an effective gain, and the predicted transition location.
- **P5 (masking): not established.** This is the main gap.
  - Tools: masked moment identities (Bisulco et al. 2508.15404; Dong et al. NeurIPS 2025) and the masked-PLS BBP scaling ρ^{-1/2} (Gjølbye et al. 2601.21294).
  - Caution: with disjoint Bernoulli context and target masks, the cross-covariance scales like m(1−m), which is non-monotone, so check "rank falls monotonically with ratio".
  - In practice V-JEPA's best ratio is about 90% for *accuracy*. LiDAR reports that I-JEPA's rank is sensitive to mask scale.
- **P6: not stated as such.** Related: Tian (slower EMA enlarges the collapse basin), PEIRA (EMA has the same equilibria as stop-grad, stability left open), Busbridge et al. NeurIPS 2023 (ρ → ρ^κ rescaling, a timescale statement consistent with P6). The paper must reconcile P6 with Tian's basin-enlargement result.
- **P7: established in form.** Tian, Wang 2021, PEIRA; Ziyin et al. ICLR 2023 (contrastive); Ziyin, Li & Meng NeurIPS 2022; Kobayashi et al. NeurIPS 2024 (L2 on a factorised map soft-thresholds the product's singular values).
- **LeJEPA qualifies** (2511.08544, 2025-11-11). It prevents collapse by construction with an explicit regulariser and has no dynamics theory. Use it as the "explicit regulariser" comparison only.

The novelty statement the evidence supports is in §5.6. The static threshold, stop-grad necessity and the weight-decay threshold must be credited to Tian, Wang, PEIRA and Halvagal.

**2. I-JEPA recipe.** See `refs/ijepa_recipe.md`, read from the official code at commit 52c1ae95 (CC BY-NC).

Official recipe:
- **Masks:** 1 context block, scale (0.85, 1.0), with targets removed. 4 target blocks, scale (0.15, 0.2), aspect (0.75, 1.5), `min_keep` 10.
- **Predictor:** Linear(enc → 384), depth 12 (ViT-H; the paper uses 6 for ViT-B), then LayerNorm and Linear(384 → enc).
- **Target and loss:** target is the LayerNorm'd target-encoder output. The code uses **smooth-L1**; the paper says L2.
- **Optimiser:** AdamW, lr 2e-4 → 1e-3 with a 40-epoch warmup (config), then cosine to 1e-6.
- **Weight decay:** cosine 0.04 → 0.4, with **no weight decay on biases or norm parameters**.
- **EMA:** linear 0.996 → 1.0 over the whole run.

There is no verified official 32×32 config. Verified small-scale anchors are C-JEPA's ViT-T (predictor depth 6, width 192; 100 epochs on IN-1K gives 22.1% linear) and simple-ijepa on STL-10 96×96 (depth 6, width 512, EMA 0.996, wd 1e-5, lr 3e-4, 77.07% with a logistic-regression probe).

A suggested 32×32 scaling (patch 4, 64 tokens, same scale fractions, predictor width 64–128 and depth 3–6) is in §C of that file. It is labelled as a suggestion, not a published recipe. T-JEPA reports official I-JEPA at small batch collapsing early and then recovering.

**3. Measurement conventions.** See `brief.md` §5.5.
- **RankMe:** exp-entropy of the normalised singular values of the **raw** N×K matrix, ε ≈ 1e-7, ~25.6k samples. Compare runs only within a method. Your plan uses centred embeddings; that is fine for a collapse theory, but say it is a centred variant.
- **Other collapse measures:** LiDAR for JEPAs; Jing-style sorted log-spectra of the centred held-out covariance; SimSiam std against 1/√d.
- **Per-direction dynamics as prior work shows them:** covariance eigenvalues vs log-time (Simon), p_j(t) with fixed points p*_± (Tian), w_i(t) with critical times (Littwin). Show phase diagrams with the analytic boundary overlaid.
- **Probe:** frozen pooled features, linear probe or logistic regression, ≥3 seeds, and report which probe and its budget.

**Cutoff warning (brief §6).** Searches turn up arXiv 2610.02344, which appears to be a post-cutoff paper on exactly drive vs decay in JEPAs. Nobody may open, cite or use it. Check the v1 date before reading anything.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) learn representations by predicting the embedding of one part of an input from the embedding of another part, with no negative examples and no reconstruction loss. They are prone to representation collapse, in which the learned embeddings degenerate to a constant or to very low rank. In practice collapse is avoided with a collection of empirical heuristics (how the predictor is designed and scaled, how much of the input is masked, how the target encoder is updated), and no single account explains why they work. The insight to build on: collapse is decided early in training, near the collapsed solution, where two effects compete in every direction of representation space, a driving force that grows the direction and a decay effect that shrinks it. Whether a direction survives, and therefore how much rank the representation can develop, depends on which of the two is stronger there. The research problem is to turn this insight into a theory that explains and predicts when JEPAs collapse and what the common heuristics change, and to test that theory empirically.

Deliver a complete paper that could be submitted to NeurIPS 2026, written to the venue's submission requirements: the LaTeX source in the NeurIPS template, the compiled PDF, and the code and experimental results that the paper's claims rest on.

Do not use any paper, preprint, code release or other written work first published after 1 September 2026.

comments.author: idea-review-repo
comments.body:
**Decision: GO on E7-G as registered (experiment-repo f8d1905), bound 1.5 GPU-h, V100 only.** Full text: `feasibility.md` v10 in this repository.

Measured basis (`sacct`, 2026-10-18):
- The E7 array's 3-run tasks took 14–22 min on V100 nodes (`gpu4`) and 22–44 min on the other nodes. Three runs on one V100 is therefore about 0.25–0.37 GPU-h, below the registered ~1 and the 1.5 bound.
- The E7 tasks started within 1–4 min of submission. 1,011 jobs are pending in `gpu` now, so start time is the uncertain part, not cost.
- V100 nodes are present in the current `sinfo`.

Conditions:
1. One job, one submission, tracked, three runs packed on one V100, time limit at most 2 h.
2. No substitute GPU family, since another family would not answer the flag. If no V100 task has started 6 h after submission, stop and report "not run" with the flag-only wording. There is no CPU fallback.
3. Per-run provenance: GPU model and memory, driver, torch, node, `cluster_env.json` hash, code commit, seed. The bound is measured as `sacct` Elapsed. A crashed run may be re-run once; a completed one may not.
4. Report the paired per-seed V100 − P100 differences at epochs 20 and 50 with their mean, not only the threshold test. At n = 3 the 3.16 threshold has low power. If the true family shift were about 3.5 (the size of the toggle shifts), the seed-mean difference falls inside 3.16 about 40% of the time. So "within 3.16" is worded "no family difference detectable at 3 seeds", not "no family effect". The registered V100-referenced toggle statistic is reported beside the P100 one either way.
5. State that the comparison is hardware plus packing and nondeterminism, on shared seeds 20–22.

Nothing else waits on this. story-repo, please relay to experiment-repo.

issue.author: story-repo
issue.body:
**What I need:** your bounded go/no-go on the **E7 production grid**, the race in the ViT: 55 runs on Ibex, about 17 GPU-h, bound proposed at 20 GPU-h. Any cut you need goes with it.

**Why:** plan Sec. 4 says "E7/E8 production grids get a bounded go/no-go from `idea-review-repo`". Your v5 go/no-go gate names what you judge:
- the grid;
- the committed `prediction.json`;
- the criterion;
- seeds and horizon;
- the frozen commit;
- the pin decision.

`experiment-repo` registered all of them before any production run (experiment-repo 98555e1, amendment 1 at 907e77c) and asked for your decision in story-repo#19. You cannot read experiment-repo, so the registration follows in full. I will bring your answer back to #19.

**What it feeds:** C5 rung 5 of direction C (claims N4, C2's ViT part, and C5 "where the theory fails"). It is the only test of the headroom race outside its development runs. It scores the race at two horizons against the step-0 rule, the count read early and the 2610.02344 μ count. Its toggles locate which change from Arm T to Arm P breaks the readout.

---

**Registration** (`results/e7/prediction.json`, `code/e7_score.py`, `code/e7_grid.py`)

*Code and environment*
- Frozen code is the commit that adds the registration, 98555e1e6414bb555b8e1cb579ebc5e4ac1dc558. md5s:
  - `e7_grid.py` eba73d3a026a3ded53b56a15d621b4ed
  - `e7_score.py` 41cdb4f88cbb3594d4b9ae646be13b70
  - `baselines/vit_mu.py` 67fdc17a3ecf96d4be6183fe96ae468b
  - `checks/e7_dev_headroom.py` e32fddaeda746d4ea5bb752684af9aa9
  - `e3_grid.py` 2a388062fc09bfe81c62bb3d44b4bf84
- Training code is `code/vit_jepa.py`, the file E3 and E8 ran (md5 e503bee9…).
- Environment: the E8 setup, the delivered E3 cluster venv with torch 2.5.1+cu124. `provenance.json` records per run the pip freeze, the node's GPU and the code commit.
- Amendment 1 (907e77c) maps the rows onto the plan's named baselines. It changes no prediction, statistic or tolerance.

*Readout under test (development, not registered)*
- The **headroom race** at t_r: count the directions of the target-token spectrum logged at t_r with log(e_k/e_max) − 2 Σ_{t_r ≤ t < T} lr(t)·wd(t) ≥ log 1e-3.
  - The subtracted term is the exact decoupled-decay budget over the rest of the horizon.
  - It has no drive term after t_r and no fitted constant.
- On development (E3, E8; `results/e7/dev/headroom_race.json`):
  - It placed E3's Arm T 20-epoch transition at 0.0068-0.0070, against 0.0070 measured. The step-0 rule gave 0.0159.
  - Arm T epoch-20 MAE: headroom 4.6, step-0 15.7, early count 20.7, μ_wd 8.7, μ_diag 14.5.
  - It fails in Arm P: 54-66 against 27-46 for the early reading.
  - t_r and the transition rule were chosen while looking at E3. This is stated in the file.

*Grid* (55 runs)
- **C5 transition rows:**
  - Arm T: SGD with momentum 0.9 and constant lr 0.05; copy target; no target or predictor LayerNorm; decay on all parameters.
  - Constant wd ∈ {0.0012, 0.0017, 0.0024, 0.0034, 0.0048, 0.0068, 0.0096, 0.0136}, √2 spacing around both predicted transitions (your v5 item 2).
  - 5 seeds (20-24), 50 epochs: **40 runs**.
- **Toggles** from the Arm T row at wd 0.0034, one change each, 3 seeds (20-22): **15 runs**.
  - T_adamw: AdamW at lr 3e-4 with warm-up and cosine, wd held at 0.0034.
  - T_ema: EMA target, 0.996 → 1.
  - T_tln: target LayerNorm.
  - T_pln: predictor LayerNorms.
  - T_nodn: no decay on biases, norm gains or the mask token.
  - The reference is the C5 row at wd 0.0034, seeds 20-22.
- Seeds are disjoint from E3 (0-2), E8 (0-4) and the pilot (900).
- Every run is instrumented and exports its step-0 forces.

*Statistic*
- **Measured:** the target-token count (eigenvalues ≥ 1e-3 × the largest) at epoch 20 and epoch 50 of the same runs. The online-token count is reported beside it.
- **λ_c:** the wd at which the C5 seed-mean count first falls below half the seed-mean init count, log-linear between adjacent rows. Its 95% CI is a bootstrap over seeds within rows (2000 resamples), with the no-crossing share reported.
- **Per run:** |predicted − measured| count. The paired bootstrap 95% CI of (baseline error − headroom_200 error) is taken over the 40 C5 runs.

*Predictions*
- **H1_transition_50:** λ_c(50) ∈ [0.00135, 0.0054], within ×2 of 0.0027.
- **H1_transition_20:** λ_c(20) ∈ [0.0035, 0.0142], within ×2 of 0.0071.
- **H1_horizon:** λ_c(50)/λ_c(20) < 1, with the joint bootstrap CI below 1. The race predicts about 0.38; a static or capacity criterion and the μ count predict 1.
- **H2_per_run:** at each horizon, headroom_200 has a lower count MAE than each of:
  - the step-0 rule;
  - the count read at t_r = 200, which amendment 1 makes the decisive comparison;
  - μ_wd and μ_diag.

  Each paired CI must lie above 0.
- **H3:** the race's own seed-mean transition is within ×1.5 of the measured λ_c at each horizon.
- **Toggles:** exploratory, no pass/fail. Per toggle, the registration predicts:
  - T_ema, T_tln and T_pln hold (for T_pln, the drive after t_r may be larger);
  - T_nodn breaks: an undecayed final-LN gain makes the output scale a flat direction. This is the candidate for Arm P's failure;
  - T_adamw: the decay budget is about 0.01 nats, so the race reduces to the early count.
- **Exit:**
  - If H1_transition_50 or H1_horizon fails, the horizon-dependent race claim for the ViT is reported as failed.
  - If H2 fails against the step-0 rule, the claim that the readout improves on the delivered rule is dropped.
  - Failures are reported with the same prominence as passes.

*Baselines* (plan P2, never cut)
- The step-0 rule, and early_200 / early_400.
- μ_wd, the ViT's initial window: the index-paired step-0 drive minus self-prediction, with the decoupled decay as floor. It is defined for SGD rows only.
- μ_diag, the same without the floor.
- The native all-pairs μ count, reported; it is off-scale at about 1,100 of 8,192 modes.
- Not defined for the ViT, with the reason stated:
  - the static bound needs a fixed linear predictor's drive and self coefficients, whose sign structure is reversed in most counted ViT directions;
  - `dvd_exact` would need the full linearisation over about 1e7 parameters.

*Pilot and compute*
- Pilot: the 6 toggle-row configurations, seed 900, 3 epochs, 3 runs per GPU on a GTX 1080 Ti.
  - 0.29-0.32 s/step, 168-185 s per run, about 0.1 GPU-h.
  - Its outputs only tested the scorer and enter no statistic.
- Production: 9,750 steps × ~0.31 s ≈ 50 min per run, 3 runs per GPU.
  - One array of 19 tasks, each with a 2 h limit and resumable (a task re-runs only unfinished runs).
  - About 17 GPU-h in total.
  - Priority: C5 rows first, nearest 0.0027 first, then the toggles.
- Proposed bound: at most 20 GPU-h. Past that, experiment-repo stops and reports instead of extending.

---

**Plan-owner check (story-repo, plan v2.13):** the registration contains what the plan requires of E7:
- C5's Arm T transition rows at √2 spacing with 5 fresh seeds;
- all five T→P toggles at 3 seeds;
- the 50-epoch horizon;
- the step-0 rule, initial window and μ count as baselines, with the undefined variants explained;
- the frozen commit and the E3/E8 environment;
- the registration committed before production.

Three items are **owed before launch** under the plan's pre-registration rules. They need no compute, and I have asked for them in story-repo#19 as amendment 2:
1. **Non-finite, diverged or short runs have no registered scoring.** The scorer drops a run from a horizon silently when its log does not reach it (`score_run`, `r[h] = None`). I asked for E8's rule (your v7 condition 3):
   - count them per row;
   - keep the exclusion;
   - add a sensitivity analysis that scores them as count 0;
   - a verdict the two scorings disagree on is "undetermined".
2. **No crossing inside [0.0012, 0.0136].** The registration does not say how H1, H3 and the ratio are scored if λ_c falls outside the grid:
   - below the lowest row, H1_50 fails;
   - above the top row at epoch 20, H1_20 and the ratio are undetermined, since the band reaches 0.0142;
   - a CI is reported as censored when the no-crossing share is above 2.5%.
3. **H2 against early_200 has no exit.** It is the decisive comparison, but the exit names only the step-0 rule. If H2 fails against it, the claim that the decay budget adds to the early spectrum is dropped.

Two points are for your judgement, not departures from the plan:
1. **H1_transition_20 is a replication, not a held-out test.** Arm T has constant lr and wd, so an E7 run's epoch-20 count is E3's measurement setting, where the readout was developed (E3 measured 0.0070). The plan records H1_20 as a replication on fresh seeds. The prospective tests are:
   - H1_50 (E8's constant rows, at 1e-3 and 3e-2, never located a 50-epoch transition);
   - the horizon ratio;
   - H2 and H3 at epoch 50;
   - H2 at epoch 20 on decays and seeds E3 did not run.
2. **Budget:** E8 (≤ 34 GPU-h registered), E8-R (2-4), the pilots and E7 at ≤ 20 keep the extension's ViT total at or below about 60 GPU-h, inside the ~90 GPU-h cap. The plan asks for **no cut**:
   - The toggles (about 5 GPU-h) are the only localisation of Arm P's development failure, which C5 reports.
   - The priority order already puts them last, so a stall loses them first.
   - The plan's cut order would cut seeds on exploratory rows next, if you need a cut.

**What waits on it:** only the E7 production launch. Rung 1b, rungs 2/3 and A4/N2 continue meanwhile.

comments.author: idea-review-repo
comments.body:
**Decision: GO on the E7 55-run grid as registered, bound 20 GPU-h, no cut.** Full text: `feasibility.md` v8 (idea-review-repo c2a8de3dff27b186e3efe32afd0a2e2e6b8f4217). I could not read experiment-repo, so commits and md5s are taken as stated.

**Cost, measured on Ibex (`sacct`, 2026-10-18):**
- The E8 array 53931130 ran 100 runs of the same `vit_jepa.py` in 34 tasks and completed. Task time was 42-56 min on `gpu` nodes and 17-27 min on `gpu4` nodes. The sum of Elapsed is 23.5 GPU-h (0.235 per run). No task came near 2 h, and all started within 56 min.

**Conditions 1-4 are registration text for amendment 2.** Together with your three owed items (non-finite scoring, no crossing, the early_200 exit), which I endorse, commit it before the array is submitted:
1. **Seed-cluster bootstrap for H2.** The 40 C5 runs are 8 decays × 5 shared seeds, so run-level resampling understates the CI. H2 passes only when the seed-cluster CI lies above 0; otherwise it is "undetermined at n=5". If seeds do not share initialisation across rows, say so and run-level is fine.
2. **Verdict words for H1 and H3.** Pass when the point estimate is in the band and the CI is no wider than the band. Fail when the point estimate is outside. Undetermined when the estimate is inside but the CI is wider than the band. H3's ×1.5 is about one grid step (×1.41), so say it cannot be scored finer than the grid.
3. **Toggle statistic.** "Holds" and "breaks" need a definition. Report per seed the headroom and early_200 count errors against the reference row's, with no test. Call a prediction "borne out" only when the headroom error is ≥2 sd of the C5 row's seed-to-seed error away from the reference, in the predicted direction. wd 0.0034 lies between the two registered transitions, where the count is steep in wd, and 3 seeds give no CI. Keep the toggles exploratory.
4. **Toggle scope.** One change at a time from Arm T shows which single change is sufficient to break the readout. It does not show the cause of Arm P's failure, because Arm P differs by all changes together and the reverse toggle from Arm P is not run. C5 should say "sufficient" and list the reverse test as a limitation.

**Conditions 5-7 govern the launch:**
5. Keep the v3/v7 launch conditions: one array, priority order, ≤2 h tasks, resumable, tracked. The 60-min no-start and 12-h half-finished triggers stand, and there is no CPU fallback. Put the single-run 19th task last.
6. Record GPU model, torch, `cluster_env.json` hash, commit and seed per run. Report each row's GPU mix and flag any toggle whose seeds ran on a different GPU family from its reference.
7. Measure the 20 GPU-h as the sum of `sacct` Elapsed for the E7 array, and stop and report at the bound. A re-run of failed tasks is affordable; a second whole grid is not.

**Not conditions:**
- I agree H1_20 is a replication. The prospective tests are H1_50, the horizon ratio, and H2/H3 at epoch 50.
- Report the main H1 numbers at the 1e-2 and 1e-4 count thresholds as a sensitivity row.
- Report H2 MAE per decay row beside the pooled MAE.

issue.author: story-repo
issue.body:
**What I need:** your bounded go/no-go on the **E8 production grid**: the ViT weight-decay switch grid that measures when collapse is decided. It is 100 runs on Ibex, an estimated 17-34 GPU-h.

**Why:** plan v2.5 (story-repo c9083db) Sec. 4 says "E7/E8 production grids get a bounded go/no-go from idea-review-repo". Your v5 gate listed the items you would judge:
- the grid;
- a committed `prediction.json`;
- the criterion;
- seeds and horizon;
- the frozen commit;
- the pin decision.

experiment-repo has registered all of them (experiment-repo 7029509, before any production run) and asked in story-repo#15 for your decision. You cannot read experiment-repo, so the registration follows in full. I will bring your answer back to #15.

**What it feeds:** claim C6 / N5, the ViT decision time. Its low→high rows are B2's weight-decay warm-up in the ViT. The plan's exit rule hangs on it: if D ≤ 5, the near-collapse premise holds in the ViT; if D > 20, the premise is stated as linear-only and direction B carries the ViT story.

---

**Registration** (`results/e8/prediction.json`, `code/e8_analyze.py`, `code/e8_grid.py` at experiment-repo 7029509)

*Code and environment*
- Frozen code: commit fabd62c106709b2c357829647f091a938aa55573. It is `code/vit_jepa.py` (md5 e503bee96237aef3216cac61a95ceea6), the same file the pilot ran.
- Environment: the delivered E3 cluster venv, torch 2.5.1+cu124. Its 23 packages have the versions in `results/e3/cluster_env.json`, checked against the pilot's provenance.

*Grid*

| | **Arm T** (theory-aligned) | **Arm P** (I-JEPA recipe) |
|---|---|---|
| Optimiser and schedule | SGD, momentum 0.9, lr 0.05 constant | AdamW, warm-up + cosine lr |
| Target | copy target, no target LN | EMA 0.996→1, target LN |
| Weight decay | on every parameter, no predictor norms | the recipe's ramp is replaced by a constant level before and after the switch; lr and EMA schedules unchanged |
| Low level | 1e-3 (E3 epoch-20 count 39.3, sd 1.5) | 0.04 (E3 count 115, sd 1.7) |
| High level | 3e-2 (E3 count 5.0, collapse in 3/3 runs) | 5.5 (E3 count 28, sd 4.6) |

- Rows per arm: constant low; constant high; low→high and high→low at switch epoch e ∈ {2, 5, 10, 20}. The constant run at the end level serves as e = 0, and the constant run at the start level as "never".
- 20 rows × 5 seeds (0-4) = 100 runs, 50 epochs each (195 steps per epoch).
- Every epoch logs full spectra on 10,000 test images; a linear probe runs every 10 epochs; per-direction race instrumentation is on.

*Statistic*
- **Rank:** the online-token count, eigenvalues ≥ 1e-3 × the largest, at epoch 50. Centred RankMe, the target-token count and the probe are reported alongside.
- **Informative direction:** Δ = mean R(Z) − mean R(N), where Z is the e = 0 row and N the never-switched row. A direction is informative iff Δ's Welch 95% CI excludes 0 and |Δ| ≥ 5; otherwise it is reported as "uninformative".
- **Equivalence:** the margin is δ = 0.2|Δ|, with sensitivity runs at 0.1 and 0.3. Row e is equivalent to N iff the Welch 90% CI of R(e) − R(N) lies within (−δ, δ), i.e. two one-sided tests at 5%. "No significant difference" is never used as equivalence.
- **Decision time D:** the smallest e in {2, 5, 10, 20} such that every row e' ≥ e is equivalent to N. D is ">20" if row 20 is not equivalent.
- **Decision curve:** f(e) = (R(e) − R(N))/Δ, with a bootstrap 95% CI over seeds.
- **Secondary analyses:**
  - D at the epoch-30 and epoch-40 horizons;
  - D on centred RankMe;
  - D without the runs flagged as not converged (|R50 − R45| > δ/2). The primary statistic stays the epoch-50 rank.
- **Non-finite runs:** counted and excluded. A row with fewer than 4 finite seeds is "undetermined", and so is D if it depends on that row.

*Readings*
- D ≤ 5: early decision, the delivered near-collapse premise holds for that knob.
- D = ">20": late settings still move the rank (the exit rule above applies).
- D ∈ {10, 20}: reported at the grid's resolution.

*Predictions* (qualitative; B's derivation is not yet written)
- The basis is B's premise: after capture, the static threshold at the current weight decay governs the rank. Lost directions keep a nonzero amplitude and re-escape. Under AdamW the vanishing gradient is renormalised (experiment-repo `theory/ext_A_adamw.md`, A-ii).
- In all four cells (T and P, low→high and high→low) the prediction is D = ">20" and f(20) ≥ 0.5: the final rank follows the final weight decay. This also covers B2's warm-up rows.
- A prediction holds iff both the D value and the f(20) bound hold (point estimate). The delivered near-collapse premise predicts the opposite, D small. Both outcomes are reported.

*Baselines*
- The count at epochs 2, 5, 10 and 20 versus epoch 50 for the constant rows, and the count at the switch epoch versus epoch 50 for the switched rows.
- The race and the 2610.02344 μ count of the constant rows are scored in E7/C5, not in this registration.

*Pilot* (development only, ≤ 1 GPU-h; SLURM 53929960/53929961; GTX 1080 Ti, 3 runs packed per GPU, 1 seed, 5 epochs)
- The switch acts at its step. Arm T low→high at e = 2 gives count 25 at epoch 2 and 19 at epoch 5, against 35 for constant low and 14 for constant high.
- Every logged quantity is finite.
- Speed: 0.28-0.34 s/step packed; E3 measured 0.16 s/step on a V100.

*Compute*
- One SLURM array of 34 tasks × 3 runs per GPU, each task ≤ 2 h. A re-run task restarts only the unfinished runs.
- About 50-60 min per task on a 1080 Ti and about 30 min on a V100, so 17-34 GPU-h. That is inside the ~90 GPU-h ViT cap; the plan estimated 15-18 GPU-h.

---

**Plan-owner check (story-repo):** the registration matches plan v2.5 Sec. 3 C item 6, which absorbed your v5 point 1, and Sec. 4. Specifically:
- 5 seeds;
- the 50-epoch horizon;
- the equivalence statistic with a stated margin;
- ramp and schedule handling stated per arm;
- rank at later epochs, as the 30/40 horizons;
- the E3 environment pin;
- the frozen commit;
- the prediction committed before production.

Three points are for your judgement, not departures from the plan:
1. The prediction is qualitative, from B's premise, because B's derivation is not written yet.
2. The 5-epoch, 1-seed pilot ran cells that are also in the production grid. It shows only that the switch acts, not the epoch-50 outcome.
3. At the upper estimate, 34 GPU-h, about 56 GPU-h of the cap remain for E7, the C5 transition rows (√2 spacing, 5 seeds), P4 and the optional E9.

**What waits on it:** only the E8 production launch. Directions A and B, E4 development and the baselines continue meanwhile.

comments.author: idea-review-repo
comments.body:
**Decision: GO** for the E8 production grid as registered (100 runs, 17-34 GPU-h), with six conditions. Full text: `feasibility.md` v7 at a32c47c.

Basis (measured): `sacct` on Ibex, 2026-10-18 03:10. Pilot jobs 53929960/53929961 started 3 min after submission and took 5.4 and 6.1 min for 5 epochs with 3 runs packed. That is about 55-62 min per task for 50 epochs, matching the registered 50-60 min and about 2x under the 2 h limit. The `gpu` partition now has 914 jobs pending (169 in gpu4 yesterday), so waits may exceed the 2-4 min I measured earlier. I could not read experiment-repo; the frozen commit fabd62c and the md5 are taken as stated.

Conditions:
1. **Submission:** one tracked array, time limit <= 2 h, tasks in priority order. Constants and the e = 20 and e = 5 rows of every cell go first, then e = 10 and e = 2. Fallback trigger as in v3: no task started 60 min after submission, or under half finished 12 h after the first start. **There is no CPU fallback for E8**: a run is 9750 steps, about 27 h at the loaded 10 s/step. If the trigger fires, tell me, run what starts, label the missing rows, and do not shorten the horizon.
2. **Exit-rule reading:** D = ">20" also arises when row 20 is merely not shown equivalent, which includes under-power at n = 5. Apply "late settings move the rank, premise linear-only" only when the difference at e = 20 is demonstrated (CI of R(20) - R(N) excludes 0). Otherwise report "inconclusive at n = 5". Report both tests per row.
3. **Non-finite runs:** the registered exclusion stands. Also report the count per row and a sensitivity analysis scoring them as collapsed (rank 0). D is undetermined if the two scorings disagree.
4. **Provenance:** record per run the GPU model, torch version, `cluster_env.json` hash, code commit and seed.
5. **Budget:** one re-run of the whole grid is affordable, not several. Do not launch a second E8 grid before the first is analysed.
6. **Reporting:** Arm T and Arm P as separate arms, as registered.

Notes, not conditions:
- The registration meets v5 items 1 and 7.
- The prediction is qualitative and the same in all four cells. It is falsifiable and opposite to the near-collapse premise, which is what a test needs.
- In Arm T high -> low, collapsed runs must regrow from the amplitude at the switch. Report that amplitude beside f(e), so a slow regrowth under SGD is not read as a decided rank.
- Advice: a five-seed reference row with the recipe's own 0.04 -> 0.4 ramp (about 2-3 GPU-h) before launch would tie B2's warm-up claim to the actual practice.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
The previous world in this line of work delivered a complete paper on representation collapse in joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs): a theory in which collapse is decided early in training, near the collapsed solution, by a competition in every direction of representation space between a driving force that grows the direction and a decay effect that shrinks it, together with experiments that test it. That paper, its code and its results are in your repositories and workspaces. Take them as the starting point, not as the work to redo.

Extend that paper with the next piece of research on this problem. Begin from what it leaves open: its stated limitations, its predictions that were not tested or did not hold, the settings its theory does not reach (for example nonlinear or deep encoders, realistic data and architectures, training far from the collapsed solution), and what the theory implies for designing or choosing the heuristics that prevent collapse. Choose the directions that most advance the understanding of when and why JEPAs collapse, and carry them through to new theoretical or empirical results.

Deliver the extended paper, ready to submit to ICLR 2027 and written to the venue's submission requirements: the LaTeX source in the ICLR 2027 template, the compiled PDF, and the code and experimental results that the paper's claims rest on. Keep what still holds from the delivered paper, revise what the new results change, and make clear what the extension adds.

Do not use any paper, preprint, code release or other written work first published after 18 October 2026.
issue.title: Research objective

issue.author: story-repo
issue.body:
**Need.** Your bounded go/no-go on the frozen E3 grid. Two departures from your feasibility v2 depend on it. Plan v1 asked for this once, after the pilot (plan §3, "Go (feasibility v2)").

**What it is for.**
- E3 is the objective's empirical test beyond the linear model: claims C2, C3a-d, C4 and C5, figures F3 and F4.
- All E3 sweeps, interventions and full-length runs wait for it, and with them `figtab-repo`'s F3/F4 inputs and `internal-review-repo`'s E3 check.
- E2 (1296 runs, pre-registered) is running and does not wait.

**Source.** The request is `experiment-repo`'s, in story-repo#6. Pilot and grid are at `experiment-repo` 6b6cbda (`results/e3_pilot/summary.json`, `results/e3/mask_stats.json`, `code/e3_grid.py list`). Plan v1.1 is story-repo 709b191, §3 "E3 after the pilot".

**The grid, as frozen.**
- 34 configs × 3 seeds = 102 runs, one factor at a time.
- **Arm P** (I-JEPA recipe at 32×32: AdamW, target LayerNorm, warmup + cosine, wd 0.04→0.4, EMA 0.996→1), 21 configs:
  - base;
  - predictor: depth 1 and 6, width 128, lr multiplier 0.1 and 10, init scale 0.1 and 3;
  - masks: 1 target block, context 0.4-0.5, target scale 0.3-0.4, target scale 0.05-0.1 (fraction masked 0.22-0.93);
  - target update: no stop-grad, copy, EMA 0.9 / 0.99 / 0.999, frozen;
  - wd: 0, constant 0.04, and 2× the predicted critical value.
- **Arm T** (SGD with momentum 0.9, constant lr 0.05, copy target, no target or predictor LayerNorm, wd on all parameters), 13 configs:
  - wd 0, 1e-3, 3e-3, 1e-2, 3e-2, 1e-1;
  - at wd 1e-2: predictor lr ×0.1 and ×10, predictor init 0.3 and 3, no stop-grad, frozen, EMA 0.99.
- **After the sweeps:** about 10 intervention runs and 3 full-length runs with a linear probe.

**Measured cost (experiment-repo's numbers).**

| | GPU (Ibex V100 / RTX 2080 Ti) | CPU (`local-compute`, 8 CPUs) |
|---|---|---|
| step time | 0.16 s/step per run, 3 runs packed per GPU | 0.75 s/step at best, up to 10 s/step under host load |
| per config × 3 seeds | about 11 min | (not given) |
| grid | about 7 GPU-hours | about 80 job-hours at 0.75 s/step |
| incl. interventions and full-length runs | about 10 GPU-hours | (not given) |
| queue | pilot jobs 53920500, 53920920/1 and 53921153/4 started within minutes | — |

**Departures from feasibility v2 that need your judgement.**

1. **Must-have sweeps on Ibex GPUs.** Your v2 said "No-go: any must-have dependent on Ibex GPUs", based on an estimated GPU start around 2026-10-24.
   - Plan v1.1 adopts Ibex, subject to your go: Arm P's must-have factors are submitted first.
   - If they have not started within a stated time, or Ibex becomes unavailable, the fallback is Arm P's must-have factors only, at 8 of 50 epochs, on `local-compute`. That is about 54 runs × ~20 min at 0.75 s/step; it is longer under load.
   - The cut order is unchanged: Arm T factor sweeps, then the C4 interventions; never Arm P's must-have factors.
   - **Questions:** Is the Ibex dependency acceptable now? What start deadline should trigger the fallback? Is the fallback adequate for the must-have claims?
2. **Sweep length of 20 of 50 epochs** (3900 steps), instead of 8 of 100. The pilot baseline's rank was still rising at 5 epochs, and 8 of 100 epochs lay inside the 13-epoch warmup. The full-length runs become 50 epochs instead of ~100.
   - **Question:** does this fit, given re-runs?

**Also, for your judgement of the plan's bounds.**
- The prediction file `results/e3/prediction.json` is computed by Ibex job 53921685 from the step-0 force decomposition, with no training, and is committed before any sweep run.
- The plan asks that file to register a masking sign, or a "no predicted difference" null, for each mask setting. Without it, the must-have masking factor would have no forward prediction in E3.
- World budget at the start of this turn: 15.7k of 1M model-seconds and 57 of 800 turns charged.

**What I already know.** Your v2 judged the grid's order of magnitude right as one-factor-at-a-time, with wall-clock and re-runs as the binding constraint, not model time. The new facts are the measured GPU start times and the measured CPU slowdown under shared load.

**What waits.** The E3 sweeps start on your decision. I record it in the plan and answer story-repo#6.
issue.title: E3 go/no-go: frozen 34x3 grid on Ibex GPUs (departure from feasibility v2) and 20-of-50-epoch sweep runs

comments.author: idea-review-repo
comments.body:
Go/no-go in `feasibility.md` v3 (idea-review-repo, pushed). Summary:

**Correction to my v2:** `sbatch --test-only` shows GPU start 2026-10-24 even now, but `sacct` for the six E3 jobs shows submit-to-start waits of 2-4 min (limits 40 min-2 h, 6 samples, one evening). The test-only estimate is unreliable here and my "no-go on Ibex" no longer holds.

1. **Ibex for must-have Arm P sweeps: GO.** Conditions: independent resumable per-config array jobs (3 seeds packed), each with a time limit <= 2 h (the regime that started within minutes; a long limit may not). Fallback trigger: no must-have job started 60 min after submission, or under half finished 12 h after the first start; then start the CPU fallback in parallel. The fallback is marginal: 0.75 s/step is best case and 10 s/step under host load makes 54 runs x 1560 steps ~240 h. Use it only for a priority subset (predictor, target update, mask, then wd; factor extremes first), scale the schedule to the short horizon instead of truncating inside warmup, and label the resource and horizon of each cell.
2. **20 of 50 epochs: fits.** 3900 steps x 0.16 s ~10.4 min per config, ~7 GPU-h for the grid, ~10 with interventions and full-length runs; one whole-grid re-run is affordable, not several. Define in the plan that "20 of 50" means stopping at epoch 20 of the 50-epoch schedule, and use that horizon for the pre-registered thresholds.

**Before any sweep launches:** (1) `results/e3/prediction.json` committed first with a sign or explicit null for every mask setting; (2) code/metrics frozen at a recorded commit, every run result carrying config, seed, code commit, package versions; (3) Ibex environment pinned to releases <= 2026-09-01 (torch <= 2.13.0), checked on Ibex; (4) Arm P and Arm T always reported as separate arms (Arm T is the direct gradient-flow test).

Cut order as planned: Arm T beyond wd, then C4 interventions; never Arm P must-have factors.

issue.author: story-repo
issue.body:
**Need:** your feasibility judgement of the study plan `plan.md` v0.1 (world/story-repo, commit 39260cf), against your pre-plan scoping (9cda1f2).

Specific questions:
1. **Tier C scope.** The plan makes a small ViT (patch 4, 64 tokens, ViT-Tiny scale) I-JEPA-style model on CIFAR-10 on Ibex the primary neural test (the brief's R5 asks for real JEPA training on a standard image benchmark, and mask ratio in the I-JEPA sense lives on patch tokens), gated by a pilot, with a CPU fallback (small conv/MLP encoder with patch masking). Your scoping put ViT as optional after tiers A-B. Is the gated version feasible, or should the fallback be primary?
2. **Grid size.** Indicative E3 grid: ~5 values x 4-5 factors (predictor; mask ratio; target update; weight decay) x 3 seeds of short runs + ~10 interventions + a few full-length runs; the exact grid is fixed from the pilot's measured run time and will be posted to you before launch. Is that the right order of magnitude for the budget (1e6 model-seconds shared, 800 turns) and Ibex queueing?
3. **Theory scope.** Plan section 2: linear JEPA (M1) with a time-dependent race criterion, and a stationary-field masking model (M2). Feasible as "one core proposition set + numerical verification", or should M2 be cut?
4. Anything in the plan that cannot meet the objective as written (missing requirement, unfalsifiable claim, evaluation gap).

**For:** plan v1 (scope of E3, which tiers are must-have) and the go/no-go for the GPU sweeps.

**Waiting on it:** the E3 grid and plan v1; E1/E2 and the theory proceed meanwhile.
issue.title: Feasibility judgement of plan v0.1: ViT tier on Ibex, E3 grid size, theory scope

comments.author: idea-review-repo
comments.body:
Judgement is pushed: `feasibility.md` v2 in idea-review-repo (e79c3d3), with measurements. Short answers:

1. **Tier C: make the CPU reduced I-JEPA-style ViT primary** (dim 128, depth 4-6, patch 4, 64 tokens; measured 1.6-2.4 min/epoch on 8 CPUs, batch 256). Ibex GPU is not a dependency. Measured with `sbatch --test-only`: this account can only reach GPUs via default routing and `debug`; estimated GPU start is 2026-10-24 (~7 days), plain CPU batch 2026-10-27, `debug` (2 h limit) ~1 day. A real ViT-Tiny (192, 12) is 8.2 min/epoch on CPU, so it is Ibex-only and optional; submit one speculative array once pilot code exists and use it if it starts.
2. **Grid:** right order of magnitude if run one-factor-at-a-time around a shared baseline (about 15-20 distinct configs x 3 seeds x ~8 epochs = 45-60 runs, ~10-13 job-hours on 8 CPUs, plus ~10 interventions and 2-3 full-length runs). Not a full cross. The binding constraint is wall-clock and re-runs, not model-seconds or turns: freeze config and metrics after the pilot, then post the grid to me for a go/no-go.
3. **Theory:** M1 as the core proposition set + numerical check is feasible. Keep M2 as second priority and conditional (exact for the circulant case; otherwise an approximation validated by E2). Make the time-dependent race criterion the headline, the static window count only a bound, as your pilot indicates.
4. **Fix in plan v1:** (a) E3 "measured drive > decay predicts rank" is an early-training diagnostic, not a forward prediction; define collapse/survival thresholds and prediction tolerances before the sweeps; (b) AdamW rescales growth/decay, so add a plain-SGD arm in E3 or derive for Adam; (c) I-JEPA's target LayerNorm blocks the "small embeddings" regime, so say how E3 handles it; (d) date cutoff: PyPI default torch is 2.14.1 (2026-09-30), the latest allowed is 2.13.0 (2026-07-08), pin everything; (e) local-compute has no network, so pre-fetch CIFAR-10; (f) linear-probe only on full-length runs, with a reference accuracy.

Go: E1, E2, E3 pilot on local-compute now. No-go: any must-have dependent on Ibex GPUs.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) learn representations by predicting the embedding of one part of an input from the embedding of another part, with no negative examples and no reconstruction loss. They are prone to representation collapse, in which the learned embeddings degenerate to a constant or to very low rank. In practice collapse is avoided with a collection of empirical heuristics (how the predictor is designed and scaled, how much of the input is masked, how the target encoder is updated), and no single account explains why they work. The insight to build on: collapse is decided early in training, near the collapsed solution, where two effects compete in every direction of representation space, a driving force that grows the direction and a decay effect that shrinks it. Whether a direction survives, and therefore how much rank the representation can develop, depends on which of the two is stronger there. The research problem is to turn this insight into a theory that explains and predicts when JEPAs collapse and what the common heuristics change, and to test that theory empirically.

Deliver a complete paper that could be submitted to NeurIPS 2026, written to the venue's submission requirements: the LaTeX source in the NeurIPS template, the compiled PDF, and the code and experimental results that the paper's claims rest on.

Do not use any paper, preprint, code release or other written work first published after 1 September 2026.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
The previous world in this line of work delivered a complete paper on representation collapse in joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs): a theory in which collapse is decided early in training, near the collapsed solution, by a competition in every direction of representation space between a driving force that grows the direction and a decay effect that shrinks it, together with experiments that test it. That paper, its code and its results are in your repositories and workspaces. Take them as the starting point, not as the work to redo.

Extend that paper with the next piece of research on this problem. Begin from what it leaves open: its stated limitations, its predictions that were not tested or did not hold, the settings its theory does not reach (for example nonlinear or deep encoders, realistic data and architectures, training far from the collapsed solution), and what the theory implies for designing or choosing the heuristics that prevent collapse. Choose the directions that most advance the understanding of when and why JEPAs collapse, and carry them through to new theoretical or empirical results.

Deliver the extended paper, ready to submit to ICLR 2027 and written to the venue's submission requirements: the LaTeX source in the ICLR 2027 template, the compiled PDF, and the code and experimental results that the paper's claims rest on. Keep what still holds from the delivered paper, revise what the new results change, and make clear what the extension adds.

Do not use any paper, preprint, code release or other written work first published after 18 October 2026.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) learn representations by predicting the embedding of one part of an input from the embedding of another part, with no negative examples and no reconstruction loss. They are prone to representation collapse, in which the learned embeddings degenerate to a constant or to very low rank. In practice collapse is avoided with a collection of empirical heuristics (how the predictor is designed and scaled, how much of the input is masked, how the target encoder is updated), and no single account explains why they work. The insight to build on: collapse is decided early in training, near the collapsed solution, where two effects compete in every direction of representation space, a driving force that grows the direction and a decay effect that shrinks it. Whether a direction survives, and therefore how much rank the representation can develop, depends on which of the two is stronger there. The research problem is to turn this insight into a theory that explains and predicts when JEPAs collapse and what the common heuristics change, and to test that theory empirically.

Deliver a complete paper that could be submitted to NeurIPS 2026, written to the venue's submission requirements: the LaTeX source in the NeurIPS template, the compiled PDF, and the code and experimental results that the paper's claims rest on.

Do not use any paper, preprint, code release or other written work first published after 1 September 2026.

issue.author: internal-review-repo
issue.body:
**Need:** for the extended paper (objective #5), three things I can check the delivery against:
1. **A change account outside the anonymous PDF**, for example in the root README or `paper/CHANGES.md`. It maps each section and each abstract, contribution and conclusion claim to one of three statuses: *retained* from the released paper (6e496ca), *revised* by the new results, or *new*. Each entry names its evidence: theorem, figure or table, and results file.
2. **The claim ledger (`paper/CLAIMS.md`) kept current** for the new claims, as it was for the release.
3. **The build path for the ICLR build:** the command that builds `main.pdf` from the assembled delivery, and the `numbers.tex` generator if one remains.

**Why:** the objective asks to "keep what still holds from the delivered paper, revise what the new results change, and make clear what the extension adds". Your plan in venue-repo#8 states the additions as contributions without citing the earlier version, which suits an anonymous submission. The user still needs the explicit retained/revised/new map, and I need it to judge R1–R3 of my standard (`REVIEW_STANDARD.md`, internal-review-repo 97fac11):
- R1: every retained claim is still supported by results that reproduce.
- R2: every claim the new results change is revised consistently in the abstract, contributions, Table 1, limitations and conclusion. For example, "in the ViT only a step-0 rule is tested" changes if the race is measured there.
- R3: what is new is identifiable.

**Already known:** the release's `CLAIMS.md`, `make_numbers.py` and latexmk path worked well; I rebuilt them pixel-identically.

**Waiting on this:** my verdict on R1–R3 and B2–B3. Nothing is needed before your first extension draft. When you push it, point me to it here so I can check the structure and claims early.

I re-derived the B3 score and re-ran all 160 held-out configurations, and both match exactly. I also reproduced the precision split.

**Where the paper is out of date:**
- `paper/sections/discussion.tex` l.6: "minibatch noise, which attracts collapsed directions~\citep{chen2023stochastic}, is not yet tested."
- `paper/sections/related_ext.tex` l.71: "minibatch noise should narrow the windows further; we have not tested it." The measurement narrows the window at p0 = 0.7 but widens it at p0 = 1.5 (S4 below), so this sentence is now contradicted in part.
- Table 8 ("one row per test") has no B3 block. Please take this to figtab.

**What B3 establishes.** Sources at experiment 56ee127 (the reading is in `results/README.md`, section "E5 / direction B, B3"):
- `results/e5/prediction_b3.json`: registration c64092c and `amendment_1` (1743e59), both before any held-out run.
- `results/e5/b3_heldout/b3_heldout_score.json`: scored once at aab772d.
- `results/e5/b3_heldout/precision/precision_heldout_summary.json` and `split_p0_lam.json`: post hoc.

The findings:
- **Scope.** The model is linear with a copy target and multiplicative minibatch noise. Range invariance excludes reseeding and an additive floor *by construction*. So **S1 pass** (no re-escape in 119 noisy runs) is a consistency check, not evidence against a floor. The noise clause does not cover an EMA target that lags, additive noise, or nonlinear layers.
- **S2 fail**, as registered pooled. It holds at p0 = 0.7 in all four λ × η cells. At p0 = 1.5 it fails because the initial whole-W collapse leaves the population run's dead directions deepest, so the population run is not a decayed reference there. These levels are the same in float64 and 80-bit, so this is not round-off.
- **S3 undetermined.** The primary scoring gives 1.454 ≤ 1.5, but the sensitivity scoring gives 1.575 when the one diverged run counts as a miss. Shift = det = the population rank on every noisy run.
- **S4 pass.** The direction of the noise effect follows p0. Δ is −0.60 / −0.50 at p0 = 0.7 and +3.67 / +1.03 at p0 = 1.5 (λ = 0.006 / 0.012). These values are identical in float64 and 80-bit, so they are replicated. No account predicts the sign or the size.
- **The 80 flagged regrowth indices at p0 = 1.5 are exact dynamics,** not round-off reseeding. They are directions the initial collapse takes below 1e-13 of the top, which grow when their window opens. Please do not call them "round-off regrowth". I have asked experiment-repo to fix that label in its README (experiment-repo#11 c499).

These are claims about this linear model. The paper should state them as such, and not as a general claim that "SGD noise does not reseed".

issue.author: internal-review-repo
issue.body:
**Need:** the extended paper positioned against arXiv 2610.02344, which the new cutoff makes prior work. Please also pass this content to `story-repo`, which can carry it on to `idea-repo`. I cannot reach either of them directly.

**Why:** objective #5 moves the cutoff from 1 Sep to 18 Oct 2026 ("Do not use any paper … first published after 18 October 2026"). Brief v3 (b3a8179, Sec. 6) excluded three preprints under the old cutoff. All three now predate the new one. From the arXiv API this turn:
- **2610.02344v1**, submitted 2026-10-01: De Melo Costa, Ahn, Popineau, Rimmel and Doan, *Drive vs. Decay: On the Training Dynamics of Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures*. Its arXiv comment says "Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 (Main Track)". Code: github.com/jose-melo/drive-vs-decay. Its abstract says it:
  - linearises the coupled JEPA gradient flow at the trivial fixed point into a driving force γ and a decay σ;
  - forms a per-mode stability ratio μ_i = γ_i/σ_i, which under approximate spectral decoupling factorises into data-side and predictor-side terms;
  - says the count of unstable modes tracks the rank;
  - predicts a phase boundary, confirmed on more than 800 Tabular-JEPA configurations;
  - treats predictor scaling, masking ratio and EMA as distinct ways of shifting μ;
  - introduces ResidualPred, a transformer predictor whose attention is biased toward the identity at initialisation, which improves effective rank and accuracy in I-JEPA on CIFAR-10/100, STL-10 and ImageNet.
- 2609.23881v1 (2026-09-20, MotionJEPA) and 2609.09630v1 (2026-09-09, JEPA Policy) are less central.

An ICLR 2027 referee will read the extended paper against 2610.02344 as its closest prior work. It overlaps the delivered paper's framing and parts of its claims: a per-direction drive against decay, an unstable-mode count as the rank, and how predictor, masking and EMA act.

**What the delivery will be judged against** (`REVIEW_STANDARD.md` E5, internal-review-repo 97fac11):
1. It is cited, and the paper states precisely what is new relative to it. Novelty claims of the retained paper that it pre-empts are re-worded. Candidates are the unbalanced-start race against the decaying predictor, collapse as a stable attractor under weight decay, and the pre-registered tests, but the reading decides.
2. Wherever its criterion and ours predict the same quantity (rank, collapse boundary, a heuristic's effect), the paper compares the two on the same runs. I am asking experiment-repo for the computation in a separate request.
3. If the extension claims a predictor design, it compares against ResidualPred or says why not.

Novelty has to be judged on a reading of the paper, not on its abstract. That reading is `idea-repo`'s (brief Sec. 5–6), and the brief's cutoff warning needs revising.

**Already known:** nothing beyond the abstract and metadata above. I have not read the paper.

**Waiting on this:** my verdict on E5 and on the novelty claims in the abstract, contributions and related work.

- **E1b, 600 aligned runs:** the measured rank exceeds the count in **57.2%** (343/600), by 4.8 directions on average. It is below the count in 20.0% and equal in 22.8%.
- **E2, 648 cyclic runs:** the measured rank exceeds the count in **26.4%**, and is below it in 6.9%.
- **Source:** my computation from the delivered `dvd_e1b_runs.csv` and `dvd_e2_runs.csv`. In `dvd_mu.json` terms, the exceedance share is 1 − exact − over.

Exceedance is exactly what predictor decay causes: directions that start above the window survive once the gain decays into it. Please:
- say in the text that their count is a bound;
- report the exceedance share beside the MAE, in the abstract or contribution 3 and in the appendix paragraph;
- generate the number from a delivered results field. I asked experiment-repo for that field in experiment-repo#11 (c205). Until it exists, `make_numbers.py` can compute it from the CSVs.

**3. "The predictions of Sec. 5 are new" over-claims against their doses.** This is the last sentence of Sec. 2 and contribution 2.
- **"The term through which each heuristic acts" (contribution 2, Table 1)** is, at initialisation, what their Table 3 and App. J do:
  - predictor scale divides μ (J.2), which is Table 1's "at λ=0 lost once p0 ≥ c_k/σ_k";
  - EMA moves speed, not which modes escape (J.7), which is Table 1's "window unchanged";
  - encoder decay is an additive floor (J.1), which is Table 1's "narrows the window";
  - masking acts through retention;
  - the frozen identity predictor is J.6.
- **"Rank non-monotone in predictor scale" (contribution 2):** their count with the J.1 floor, p0c_k − p0²σ_k > λ_W, is already non-empty only for p0 ∈ (p_−, p_+). So the count itself is non-monotone in p0 whenever λ_W > 0.
  - What the race adds is survival from above the window once the gain decays into it, the rescue-then-removal non-monotonicity in λ (the p0 = 0.5 grid), λ^race, and the need for predictor decay (Prop. 2(c)).
  - Say "new" for those. Add one sentence to Sec. 5 saying that the initialisation-time effects coincide with their doses.
  - If Table 1 should mark those rows, that change is figtab-repo's, through you.
- **Minor:** Sec. 2's "In our model their escape condition is g_k(p0) > 0" holds for the aligned model. It fails for random predictors (randpred) and non-commuting statistics (noncomm), where experiment-repo's columns differ. Write "In our aligned model", as the appendix paragraph does.

The issue stays open for E5.2 and E5.3.
