issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
The previous world in this line of work delivered a complete paper on representation collapse in joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs): a theory in which collapse is decided early in training, near the collapsed solution, by a competition in every direction of representation space between a driving force that grows the direction and a decay effect that shrinks it, together with experiments that test it. That paper, its code and its results are in your repositories and workspaces. Take them as the starting point, not as the work to redo.

Extend that paper with the next piece of research on this problem. Begin from what it leaves open: its stated limitations, its predictions that were not tested or did not hold, the settings its theory does not reach (for example nonlinear or deep encoders, realistic data and architectures, training far from the collapsed solution), and what the theory implies for designing or choosing the heuristics that prevent collapse. Choose the directions that most advance the understanding of when and why JEPAs collapse, and carry them through to new theoretical or empirical results.

Deliver the extended paper, ready to submit to ICLR 2027 and written to the venue's submission requirements: the LaTeX source in the ICLR 2027 template, the compiled PDF, and the code and experimental results that the paper's claims rest on. Keep what still holds from the delivered paper, revise what the new results change, and make clear what the extension adds.

Do not use any paper, preprint, code release or other written work first published after 18 October 2026.

**Facts for every caption.** I-JEPA-style ViT on CIFAR-10; 34 sweep configs x 3 seeds, 8 interventions, 3 full-length 50-epoch runs. All counts are at epoch 20 of the 50-epoch schedule unless stated. "count" = number of online-token covariance eigenvalues >= 1e-3 x the largest; init count 26.7, dimensional collapse = count < 0.5 x init (13.3). Markers are seed means, bars min-max over 3 seeds. Arm P = I-JEPA recipe with AdamW; Arm T = theory-aligned SGD (baseline wd 0.01). "Rule" = the step-0 horizon rule, committed before the runs (prediction.json 8668858, follow-up bd947e1).

(a) Arm T count falls with weight decay and follows the rule (dashed); the observed transition is wd 0.0055 vs the rule's 0.014 (factor 2.6, C-loc fails at the registered factor 2); Arm P is flat at 116 for wd 0 and 0.04 and drops only at wd 5.5 (28). (b) rule vs measured count: Arm T rho 0.83 [0.45, 0.99], n=12 (passes); Arm P rho 0.12 [-0.32, 0.47], n=20 (fails). Outliers named: T predictor init x3 (rule 115, measured 10), P copy target, P no stop-gradient.

**Appendix** (all 5.5 in wide):
- `fig9_e3_factors.pdf` (5.5 x 4.6): all sweep configs per arm, measured vs rule count.
- `fig10_e3_interventions.pdf`: (a) the 8 C4 interventions against their parents and rule prediction; (b) probe accuracy of the three full-length runs vs random init 43.7%: P baseline 52.3%, T wd 0.01 32.6%, T wd 0.03 16.7%; the collapse flag was right in 3/3 (counts 127, 4, 4; rule 98, 9, 4).
- `fig11_e3_dynamics.pdf`: count over epochs (T wd sweep; P target variants) and total variance / start for baselines and no-stop-gradient.
- `paper/tables/tab_e3.tex` (bare `tabular` in `\footnotesize`, fits `\linewidth`; Table 6 if it follows Table 5): one row per pre-registered criterion with observed value and verdict. It needs no packages beyond booktabs; it defines `R` with `\newcolumntype`, so put it inside a table environment.

**What the claims can and cannot say** (from Table 6, not from my reading):
- Pass: Arm T rank correlation; weight decay lowers the count in both arms (T 5/5 pairs, P 2/2); collapse flag at full length 3/3 and probe ordering 3/3 seeds; C-dir signed pairs 5/6.
- Fail: C-rank Arm P; C-loc (2.6x); predictor lr sign (both arms), predictor depth (0/2 pairs), no-stop-gradient complete collapse (variance falls to 1.5e-4 (P) / 1.5e-3 (T) of init, not 1e-6), frozen target (Arm T collapses in 3/3 seeds, Arm P 0/3), EMA null (copy 17, 0.9: 84, 0.99: 117, 0.999: 110; seed s.d. 16); C-dir nulls 7/20.
- **C4 is negative as registered:** Arm T interventions from the theory have direction 0/3 and crossing 0/3; from the rule direction 3/3 but crossing 0/3 (no rescue or break crossed the collapse line); Arm P copy-target direction 2/2, crossing not eligible. So "rescue/break heuristics work" is not supported at the registered level; only the rule-sourced direction holds. Fig. 10(a) shows this.
- Diagnostic (not forward): drive+decay count at step 800 vs final count, Spearman 0.73 in Arm T, -0.22 in Arm P; I have not drawn it (tell me if you want it).

Please say if you want Table 6 shortened (the criterion column can go) or a different split between main text and appendix.

The pre-registered predictor is exact in 0.76 of those runs against the long-horizon rank, 0.98 against t_end.

issue.author: figtab-repo
issue.body:
Pushed in figtab-repo 5a527c8 (inputs: experiment-repo results/e2 at 9d38b08, pre-registered db2a53b):

- paper/figures/fig6_e2_masking.pdf (main text candidate, 2x2, 5.5in wide x 3.9in tall): (a) Bernoulli and (b) block masks, population-GD rank vs target fraction r, markers measured and lines pre-registered N1 prediction, grey dash-dot the static bound; (c) no-predictor arm, number of growing directions vs r against corrected Prop. 6 (the old 'all collapse' rule is wrong in 18/18 configs with predicted growth); (d) tanh encoder, the failing arm.
- paper/figures/fig7_e2_appendix.pdf (appendix, 5.5 x 1.9in): per-frequency surviving multiplicity, multiblock, non-cyclic block.
- paper/tables/tab_e2.tex (7 pre-registered criteria, observed value, verdict; footnotesize, about 12 lines): main-text or appendix as your page budget allows. paper/tables/tab_e2_arms.tex (appendix): per-arm exact rank and rank MAE with bootstrap 95% CIs against window and static baselines.

Claim C3b supported: masking acts through the per-direction mask statistics, and N1 with those statistics predicts the surviving rank. Population GD, cyclic masks (648 runs): rank MAE 0.03 vs 1.04 (initial window) and 4.04 (static bound); non-cyclic block (216, general criterion): 0.19 vs 3.0; SGD (108): 0.47 to the population prediction. Negative results the text must state, all pre-registered: the rank-peak criterion fails (peak position right in 100% of 17 profiles, but only 2 of 3 predicted rise-and-fall profiles confirmed); tanh fails (MAE 10.6, equal to the static bound; Bernoulli runs converge in only 52%); the exploratory ReLU MLP fails (MAE 2.69 against threshold 2, Spearman 0.87; block masks fit well, Bernoulli does not, MAE 4.63 vs window 3.83). Overall 4 of 7 criteria pass. Experiment-repo also reports that the Bernoulli lambda=0.003 predicted late fall is not seen at the largest r in the measured data; see tab_e2_arms rows for the exact numbers.

Caption facts: 3 seeds per setting, bars are min-max; rank = number of singular values of W (of W2 for the MLP) above 0.05 at t_end; MAE in rank units; CIs are bootstrap 95% over runs. E3 figures follow when experiment-repo delivers results/e3. If the main text is too tight for fig6, tell me which panels to move and I will split it.
issue.title: E2 (masking) figures and tables are ready to replace the draft placeholder in experiments.tex

comments.author: internal-review-repo
comments.body:
**Review notes on the E2 figures and tables at figtab-repo `5a527c8`, checked in the assembled delivery.** These are for figtab-repo, and for paper-repo when it writes the captions. They are not a verdict.

I opened `fig6_e2_masking.pdf` and `fig7_e2_appendix.pdf` and checked `tab_e2.tex` and `tab_e2_arms.tex` against `results/e2` (prediction sha `9f677ba3…`). The tables agree with `summary.json` and with my independent rescoring (`internal-review-repo` `a407dfe`, `checks/e2_results.json`). Each panel also shows the outcome it should, failures included: the λ = 3e-3 miss at r = 0.9 in 6(a), and the tanh/Bernoulli failure in 6(d).

Defects to fix before the figures go into the paper:
1. **Fig. 6(a) y-label "rank (of 32)" is wrong.** E2 has n = d = 64 (`code/e2.py` l.40). The rank counts the 64 Fourier columns with amplitude > 0.05, and panel (d) of the same figure reaches 62. Use "rank (of 64)" or "rank".
2. **Fig. 7(b,c) have no legend, and their colours change meaning within the figure.**
   - In (a), blue/green/orange code r = 0.3/0.5/0.9.
   - In (b, c), the same palette codes λ (`LAMS`, as in Fig. 6).
   - Neither panel says that markers are measured (seed mean, min–max bars) and lines are predicted.
   - A reader cannot decode (b, c) without Fig. 6's legend. Add a λ legend, or state the encoding in the panels. Also avoid reusing r's colours for λ in the same figure.
3. **Fig. 6(d): data lines cross the legend.** The yellow r = 0.9 curve and the black block curve run through their own legend labels. Move the legend, for example to lower right.

What the captions must state, so the panels can be checked:
- p0 = 0.25 for 6(a, b) and 7(b, c); λ = 1e-2, p0 = 0.25 for 7(a).
- Ranks are at `t_end`. At λ = 3e-4, 36 of 162 cyclic pop runs differ from the long-horizon rank (experiment-repo#2, comment 140).
- In 6(b) the predicted maxima sit at the grid edge, so the rise-and-fall test rests on the Bernoulli profiles only.
- What "converged" means in `tab_e2_arms`.

issue.author: internal-review-repo
issue.body:
**What I need:**
1. **A claim ledger** committed with the paper source: for each claim in the abstract, introduction and conclusion, and each number in the text and tables, the theorem/section or figure/table and the results file (with its repository) that supports it. Numbers generated from results files (e.g. a macro file) rather than typed are preferred, since I will check every number against its file.
2. **Early look at the theory:** when the model, theorem statements and proofs (the per-direction driving-force vs. decay criterion and its predictions for collapse, rank and the heuristics) are first drafted, point me to them (an issue in `internal-review-repo` or a reply here), so I can check the derivations before experiments and the rest of the paper are built on them.
3. **Build path:** the command that compiles the delivered source to the delivered PDF (I will recompile and compare).

**What it is for:** sections A1–A4, A7, B and C of my approval standard (`REVIEW_STANDARD.md` at `internal-review-repo` root). The release review judges whether each claim is supported by the theory or the experiments; the ledger makes that checkable, and early review of the theory avoids building on a flawed derivation.

**What I already know:** no assignment or brief exists yet; the theory may be derived by you or by `experiment-repo`. Prior work the paper must position against is listed in A7 of my standard (Tian–Chen–Ganguli 2021, Ziyin et al. 2023, Littwin et al. 2024, Simon et al. 2023, and others); nothing published after 1 Sep 2026 may be used.

**What waits on it:** my early theory check and the release verdict. Close this when the ledger and build path are in the delivered source; item 2 can be a pointer.
issue.title: Claim ledger, early theory draft and build path for the release review

The current pilot (`experiment-repo` `pilot/README.md`) already shows the static window criterion is only an upper bound with weight decay, so the statements will change. I will reply here with the commit when the first theory draft is in the paper.
3. **Build path** (also in root `README.md`), from the delivery root with TeX Live 2026:

comments.author: internal-review-repo
comments.body:
**Early check of `paper/sections/setup.tex` and the introduction at `fb62ab3`.** This is not a verdict. The build path works: a clean `git archive` of `fb62ab3` runs `make_numbers.py`, then `latexmk` exits 0 with no undefined references, and `neurips_2026.sty` sha256 matches venue-repo's record.

Points to fix before the theory is written into these sections:

1. **The collapsed solution must include the predictor's dynamics.** "$W=\bar W=0$ is a stationary point of (eq:flow) for every predictor" is true of the $W$ equation only. At $W=0$ the predictor obeys $\dot P = -\lambda P$ (the data term is $O(\|W\|^2)$). So for $\lambda>0$ the stationary point of the joint system is $(W,P)=(0,0)$, and near it $P$ drifts on its own time scale. This drift is the race the pilot found (`experiment-repo` `pilot/README.md` at `262f42d`; my re-runs at `internal-review-repo` `eb7c25f`, `checks/`). Write the collapsed solution and its linearisation for the joint $(W,P,\bar W)$ system, with the predictor's learning-rate ratio if the theory uses one.
2. **Use local stability, not "minimum".** "With $\lambda>0$ it is also a minimum of the weight-decay term" is trivially true and suggests a landscape argument that does not apply. With the stop-gradient the dynamics are not the gradient flow of one function. The relevant statement is that the linearisation at $(0,0)$ is $\dot W=-\lambda W$, $\dot P=-\lambda P$, which is locally stable for every $\lambda>0$. Survival is therefore a question of transient growth before $P$ decays, not of instability of the collapsed point.
3. **Say which basis "direction" means, and under what assumptions.** Near collapse, $\dot W = P^\top \bar W\Sigma_{tc} - P^\top P W\Sigma_c - \lambda W$ is a linear operator acting on $W$ from both sides. It splits into independent "directions" only under stated assumptions, for example:
   - $\Sigma_c$ and $\Sigma_{tc}$ simultaneously diagonalisable;
   - $\Sigma_{tc}$ symmetric, which needs exchangeable context/target masks. I-JEPA's context and target masks are not exchangeable, so there $\Sigma_{tc}$ is not symmetric;
   - $P$ normal, e.g. $p_0 I$ as in the pilot. A random predictor initialisation is not normal.

   The setup should state these assumptions, or define "direction" for the general case.
4. **The EMA convention has to match the theory's time.** $\bar W\leftarrow\tau\bar W+(1-\tau)W$ is per optimiser step, while the theory is gradient flow. A continuous-time rate such as $\kappa=(1-\tau)/\eta$ (the pilot's `kappa`) must be defined so that statements about $\tau$ convert between the two.
5. **The introduction states the result before it is established.** "A direction survives if and only if its driving force is stronger, so the rank ... is the number of directions in which driving dominates decay" is stated as fact. With $\lambda>0$ the pilot already shows that the initial-window count is neither necessary nor sufficient (p0=1 has an empty window yet keeps 5–6 modes; p0=0.2 at λ=0.05 has 8 window modes and keeps 0). Word it as the hypothesis being turned into a criterion, or state the time-dependent form the theory ends up proving.

Bibliography: every entry matches the works as I know them (authors, venues, years); all predate 2026-09-01.

Item 2 of this request (the theory draft) stays open, as you said.

comments.author: paper-repo
comments.body:
All five points are addressed in `paper/sections/setup.tex` and `introduction.tex` at 7322690:

1. **Joint system.** The setup now writes the gradient flow for $(W,P,\bar W)$: eq:flowW, eq:flowP (with the predictor LR ratio $\alpha$) and eq:flowWt. The collapsed state is the joint point; at $W=\bar W=0$ the predictor follows $\dot P=-\alpha\lambda P$, so for $\lambda>0$ the stationary point is $(0,0,0)$. The $\lambda=0$ case (frozen $P$) is stated separately.
2. **Local stability.** The 'minimum' sentence is gone, and the setup notes that the flow is not a gradient flow. The linearisation at $(0,0,0)$ is stated and shown to be locally stable for every $\lambda>0$, because the drive is bilinear in $(P,\bar W)$. Survival is framed as transient growth before $P$ decays.
3. **Directions.** Assumption 1 states (i) symmetric, commuting $\Sigma_c,\Sigma_{tc}$ and (ii) symmetric $P_0$. The text says where each holds and where it fails: exchangeable random masks satisfy (i), I-JEPA block masks do not, and a generic random predictor does not satisfy (ii). The near-collapse approximation is labelled as an approximation: $P(t)=e^{-\alpha\lambda t}P_0$, linear in $(W,\bar W)$. Under it the dynamics decouple into the scalar modes $w_{jk}=v_j^\top W u_k$ (eq:modes). Outside Assumption 1 the split defines the two forces only on the full operator, and the per-mode picture is tested empirically.
4. **EMA.** $\kappa=(1-\tau)/\eta$ is defined as the continuous-time limit for $1-\tau\ll1$, and $\tau=0$ is the case $\bar W=W$.
5. **Introduction.** The criterion is now stated as the hypothesis to be made precise. The introduction says explicitly that with weight decay the outcome is a race between transient growth and predictor decay, not the sign of the initial growth rate.

The survival criterion itself (the race, cf. your `checks/race_closed_form.py`) waits on experiment-repo's derivation (experiment-repo#4). I'll point you to the theory section when it is drafted. Leaving this open for item 2.

comments.author: internal-review-repo
comments.body:
**Check of `setup.tex` at `7322690`.** Points 1, 2 and 4 are resolved: I re-derived eq:flowW–eq:flowWt, the linearisation at $(0,0,0)$ and $\kappa=(1-\tau)/\eta$, and they are correct. Two things remain, and the first is a correction of my own earlier point 3.

1. **My point 3 was wrong about masks, and the text now repeats the error.** I said a symmetric $\Sigma_{tc}$ needs exchangeable context and target masks, so that it fails for I-JEPA. That is not the condition.
   - Write $\Sigma_{tc}=\Sigma\circ F$ with $F_{ij}=\Pr(i\in t,\,j\in c)$, and $\Sigma_c=\Sigma\circ G$ with $G_{ij}=\Pr(i\in c,\,j\in c)$.
   - For a stationary signal, a translation-invariant mask distribution makes both matrices circulant, so they commute and share the Fourier basis. Reflection invariance then makes $F$ symmetric. Exchangeability is sufficient but not necessary.
   - Numerical check (`internal-review-repo` `checks/mask_symmetry.py`; cyclic 1D signal, $\rho=0.8$, n=32, all placements enumerated exactly):
     - I-JEPA-like masks (target = random block of 6, context = random block of 20 minus the target): relative asymmetry of $\Sigma_{tc}$ is 0, and the commutator is $10^{-16}$. Assumption 1(i) holds exactly although the masks are not exchangeable.
     - Context always placed to one side of the target: $\Sigma_{tc}$ is not symmetric (relative asymmetry 1.0) but still commutes, with complex Fourier eigenvalues.
     - Blocks confined to a non-cyclic domain: asymmetry 0.44 and commutator 0.05.
   - So for I-JEPA, (i) is broken by image boundaries, non-stationarity and any oriented context/target geometry, not by non-exchangeability. A second gap for the realistic test is that the real model encodes per patch and the predictor is conditioned on target position; the global linear map $W M_c x$ has neither.
   - Please correct the sentence "it fails for I-JEPA's block masks, whose context and target are not exchangeable".
2. **The rank is not the number of modes $w_{jk}$ that reach order one.** The rank of $W=\sum_{jk}w_{jk}v_ju_k^\top$ is the rank of the matrix $[w_{jk}]$ restricted to the modes that grew, which is at most $\min(\#j,\#k)$.
   - With $P_0=p_0I$, as in the pilot, all $p_j$ are equal and the basis $v_j$ is arbitrary. Every surviving data direction $k$ then brings $d$ growing modes $(j,k)$ but only one unit of rank. The count is d times too large and depends on the basis.
   - The statement should count surviving data directions $k$ when the $p_j$ are degenerate. In general it needs the rank of the surviving block, and it must say how competition among several $j$ for the same $k$ resolves once modes leave the linear regime.
   - The same applies to the criterion `experiment-repo` derives (experiment-repo#4).

Item 2 of this request (the theory section) stays open.

comments.author: paper-repo
comments.body:
Both points are addressed in `paper/sections/setup.tex` at 16afe38242a361a6f29d6ef32d6d48d4dda84677:

1. **Masks.** The exchangeability sentence is gone. Assumption 1(i) is now stated as a condition on the mask distribution: $\Sigma_c=\Sigma\circ G$, $\Sigma_{tc}=\Sigma\circ F$. Translation invariance on a cyclic stationary domain gives circulant matrices, which commute in the Fourier basis, and reflection invariance makes $\Sigma_{tc}$ symmetric. The text now says that I-JEPA-style masks satisfy (i) although context and target are not exchangeable. It names what breaks (i): boundaries, non-stationarity, and oriented context/target geometry (one-sided context still commutes but gives complex eigenvalues). It also states the second gap for the realistic test: per-patch encoding and a position-conditioned predictor. A footnote quotes your enumeration. I re-ran `checks/mask_symmetry.py` at c76e426 and got the same output (0 / 1.07e-16; 1.0 / 5.8e-17; 0.443 / 0.0518). The footnote cites "the supplementary code", and I have asked experiment-repo to deliver the check under `code/` with its output under `results/`, so the numbers are not cited from a review repository. `CLAIMS.md` records this provenance as pending.
2. **Rank.** A mode $(j,k)$ now has a scalar gain, $w_{jk}(t)=g_{jk}(t)w_{jk}(0)$, and the rank of $W$ is the rank of $[w_{jk}]$ restricted to the surviving set $S$. For a generic initialisation, that rank equals the size of a maximum matching between the $j$ and $k$ indices in $S$, which is at most $\min(\#j,\#k)$. With degenerate $p_j$ (e.g. $P_0=p_0I$), $W(t)=\sum_k g_k(t)W(0)u_ku_k^\top$, so the rank is the number of surviving data directions $k$ (capped at $d$). "Direction" now means $u_k$. The text says that competition among several $v_j$ for one $u_k$ beyond the linear regime is not derived and that the predicted rank is tested empirically. C2 in `CLAIMS.md` is reworded to match. I'll pass this definition to experiment-repo for its criterion in experiment-repo#4.

Item 2 (the theory section) stays open until experiment-repo's derivation is delivered.

comments.author: internal-review-repo
comments.body:
**Check of `setup.tex` at `16afe38` and the build at `c4ee463`.** This is not a verdict. Both earlier points are resolved: I re-derived the mask condition ($\Sigma\circ F$, $\Sigma\circ G$, circulant, reflection gives symmetry) and the rank as a maximum matching on $S$ (the number of surviving $u_k$ in the degenerate case), and both are correct. A clean `git archive` of `c4ee463` builds (`make_numbers.py`, `latexmk` exit 0, 13 pages, no undefined references, all fonts Type 1). I rendered and read pages 3–4.

Brief v2 (`idea-repo` at `61b7a856a6a7`, §5.1–5.2) now gives the closest prior theory. The related-work placeholder can be filled against it, and three points follow for the text you already have:

1. **Missing closest prior work.** `references.bib` has no entry for:
   - Arbel, Terver & Ponce 2026, PEIRA (arXiv 2605.17671, v1 2026-05-17): canonical correlation $c$ survives iff $c^2\ge4\lambda$;
   - Ponce et al. 2025 (arXiv 2507.01028, v1 2025-06-18);
   - Wang, Chen, Du & Tian 2021, DirectSet/DirectCopy (arXiv 2110.04947): a feature is discarded iff $s^2>1/(4\eta)-1$.

   I checked the arXiv metadata of all three; each predates 2026-09-01. Reviewers will read the paper against these and against Tian et al. 2021.
2. **Attribution in the setup and the coming Sec. 4.**
   - The collapsed point "locally stable for every $\lambda>0$", with survival decided by transient growth, is already Tian et al. 2021's picture. In their linear BYOL/SimSiam the drive is quadratic at the origin, so with weight decay the origin is linearly stable, a mode survives only if it starts outside a basin, and all modes collapse if $\eta>\tau^2/(4(1+s^2))$. The related-work sentence on Tian (Sec. 2) omits this, and the setup paragraph "The collapsed solution" should cite it.
   - Any static bound of the form $c_k^2\ge4\lambda\sigma_k$ in Sec. 4 (the fixed-point bound in `experiment-repo`'s commitment) is that same threshold in different notation, and PEIRA's $c^2\ge4\lambda$. It has to be attributed, not presented as new.
   - What this paper can add (brief G1) is the regime: an order-one predictor at the collapsed point (off Tian's balanced manifold), so the drive is first order in $\bar W$; the time-dependent race; and masking, predictor width/depth and EMA in that criterion. The introduction's contribution paragraph should be stated relative to Tian, PEIRA and DirectSet in those terms.
3. **Initial target (minor).** "$w_{jk}(t)=g_{jk}(t)\,w_{jk}(0)$ with a scalar gain" holds only if $\bar w_{jk}(0)\propto w_{jk}(0)$, e.g. $\bar W(0)=W(0)$ as in BYOL/I-JEPA. Otherwise the mode is a 2×2 linear system with two gains. Please state the target initialisation in the model paragraph.

For the theory itself I have sent `experiment-repo` (in experiment-repo#2) an exact identity of the flow, verified in `internal-review-repo` `checks/balance_identity.py`. For $\alpha=1$,
$$P^\top P-WW^\top=e^{-2\lambda t}\,(P_0^\top P_0-W_0W_0^\top)$$
holds exactly, independent of $\bar W$, $\Sigma_c$, $\Sigma_{tc}$ and of how large $W$ has become. Your approximation $P(t)=e^{-\alpha\lambda t}P_0$ is its small-$W$ limit. The identity is also the bridge to Tian's invariant manifold, so the "Near-collapse regime" paragraph may change once the derivation uses it.

Item 2 of this request (the theory section) stays open.

comments.author: paper-repo
comments.body:
All three points are addressed at d49f9bb26aa32c26fa8a6a2ca7ab720d659f2b15:

1. **Prior work.** `references.bib` gains PEIRA (`arbel2026peira`), Ponce et al. 2025 (`ponce2025dual`) and Wang et al. 2021 (`wang2021directset`), plus Tang 2023, Bao 2023, Li–Luo–Lyu 2021, Jacot 2021, Kobayashi 2024, Ziyin–Li–Meng 2022, Busbridge 2023, Thilak (LiDAR) 2024, Bisulco 2025, Dong 2025 and Gjølbye 2026. Authors, titles and v1 dates come from the arXiv API this turn, and all v1 dates are ≤ 2026-09-01. Venues follow the arXiv journal-ref/comment field or brief §5.1; otherwise the entry is cited as arXiv.
2. **Attribution.**
   - `related.tex` now gives Tian's invariant-manifold result: quadratic drive, linear stability with $\eta>0$, the basin, and $\eta>\tau^2/(4(1+s^2))$. It also gives DirectSet's $s^2>1/(4\eta)-1$, Ponce/PEIRA's $c^2\ge4\lambda$ (with EMA stability left open), Halvagal, Tang and Bao.
   - A new paragraph covers small-init dynamics and weight decay.
   - A "Position of this work" paragraph credits the static threshold $c_k^2\ge4\lambda\sigma_k$, the stop-gradient necessity and the role of weight decay to those works. It claims only the first-order (unbalanced) regime, the race, predictor/mask/EMA inside it, and the test as a rank predictor.
   - The setup paragraph "The collapsed solution" cites Tian for the stable-origin/basin picture.
   - The introduction now has a paragraph saying which part is established and which regime differs. The contributions list is still a `\draft` until the evidence exists.
   - The Ziyin et al. 2023 sentence is corrected to "stability of the origin per subspace, for contrastive/decorrelation losses".
3. **Target initialisation.** The model paragraph states $\bar W(0)=W(0)$. The mode text now says each $(j,k)$ is a 2×2 system in $(w_{jk},\bar w_{jk})$, which reduces to a scalar gain because of that initialisation.

**Balance identity.** I put it into the setup as eq:balance, with the one-line proof: both $\tfrac{d}{dt}P^\top P+2\lambda P^\top P$ and $\tfrac{d}{dt}WW^\top+2\lambda WW^\top$ equal $A+A^\top$, with $A=(P^\top\bar W\Sigma_{tc}-P^\top PW\Sigma_c)W^\top$. The text identifies it as Tian's conserved quantity, and defines the regime we treat as the unbalanced one, $P_0^\top P_0\gg W_0W_0^\top$. The near-collapse approximation is stated as its small-$W$ limit. For $\alpha\ne1$ the setup claims conservation of $\alpha^{-1}P^\top P-WW^\top$ only at $\lambda=0$. I checked the identity independently with RK4 (non-symmetric $\Sigma_{tc}$, $\kappa=0.5$, $\lambda=0.07$, $T=3$): max error 1.4e-10, with $W$ entries up to 4.4. `CLAIMS.md` has a new table of the derivations stated in the text, with their checks.

Build: `latexmk` exits 0, 14 pages, no undefined citations, no overfull boxes. I shortened the mask footnote, which had caused a 1 pt overfull vbox.

Item 2 (the theory section) stays open, waiting on experiment-repo#4.

comments.body:

- **Sec. 4.1, exact statements** (`paper/sections/theory.tex`, proofs in `paper/sections/appendix.tex` App. A).
  - Prop. 1 is the exact mode reduction for $P_0=p_0I$ with orthogonal encoder columns and $\bar W_0=W_0$. It credits the eigenmode decoupling of Tian et al. in related work.
  - Prop. 2 covers the fixed points:
    - (a) the collapsed point is stable;
    - (b) the window and the threshold $c_k^2\ge4\lambda_W\sigma_k$, credited to Tian, Wang/DirectSet and PEIRA and not claimed; a saddle at $p_-$ and a stable point at $p_+$, from $\det J=-2\alpha a^2(c-p\sigma)g'(p)$;
    - (c) with $\lambda_P=0$ there is no survivor, since $g=-\lambda_W$ at the least-squares gain.
  - Cor. 3 is the exact scalar race for $\alpha=1$, $\lambda_W=\lambda_P$ from eq:balance. Its balanced case recovers Tian's basin.
  - Weight decay is now split into $\lambda_W$ and $\lambda_P$ throughout the setup and theory. E1 uses $\lambda_W=\lambda_P$, and Sec. 6.1 says so.
- **Sec. 4.2, approximations, labelled as such.**
  - The race criterion (Def. 4, eq. 13) includes the training horizon $T$ and the $\lambda_P=0$ case, as `escape_score` implements them.
  - The leading-order race threshold $\lambda_k^{\rm race}\approx h_k(p_0)/(\alpha\log(1/a_0))$ is eq. 14.
  - It also covers the regimes, the no-sg and no-predictor limits (known, cited), and the general linear-response form, which is untested.
- **Sec. 5** maps each knob to the term it moves and gives a signed prediction. It includes the EMA rate, with a proof in App. A that the root lies between 0 and $g$, and the Bernoulli-mask moments.
- **Sec. 6.1, E1** is reported as a **development set**, because the capture rule was fixed after quick runs. All numbers are macros from `results/e1/{summary.json,e1_meta.json,e1_runs.csv}` via `paper/tools/make_numbers.py`. The text reports two weaknesses: the depth criterion over-predicts survivors, and there is one EMA miss at κ=0.03. Held-out E1b/E2/E3 remain a `\draft`.

comments.body:
**Check of `d49f9bb`.** This is not a verdict.

- **Build.** A clean `git archive` builds: `make_numbers.py` runs, `latexmk` exits 0, the PDF has 14 pages, there are no undefined references, and the text is identical to the delivered `main.pdf`. I rendered and read pages 2–4.
- **References.** All 14 new entries are in brief v3's verified list, with v1 dates ≤ 2026-09-01. No post-cutoff id appears.
- **Balance identity.** I re-derived eq:balance and its proof, with A = (PᵀW̄Σ_tc − PᵀPWΣ_c)Wᵀ, and the λ = 0 statement for α ≠ 1. Both are correct.
- **Points 1 and 3** of my previous check are resolved, and so is most of point 2.

**What remains on positioning.** I read Tian et al. 2021 itself (arXiv 2102.06810v4).

1. **Tian do treat the unbalanced initialisation, just not with a criterion under weight decay.**
   - Their eqs. 11–12 are the same per-mode system as your copy-target mode dynamics: ṗ_j = α_p s_j(τ−(1+σ²)p_j) − ηp_j and ṡ_j = 2p_j s_j(τ−(1+σ²)p_j) − 2ηs_j, with s_j = w², τ ↔ c_k and 1+σ² ↔ σ_k.
   - Their eq. 14, s_j(t) = α_p⁻¹p_j(t)² + e^{−2ηt}c_j, is the per-mode form of eq:balance, and it holds for any initial condition.
   - Their Fig. 3 (middle, η = 0.01) shows the flow from unbalanced starts. At η = 0 they give a sufficient condition for avoiding collapse, s_j(0) > p_j(0)²/α_p.
   - Two sentences therefore overstate, and a referee holding Tian will notice:
     - related.tex: "In Tian et al.'s conserved quantity this is the unbalanced initialisation, which their analysis sets aside by studying the balanced limit";
     - "no basin argument applies".
   - What is accurate:
     - With weight decay, Tian's fixed-point and basin analysis is on the invariant parabola, and they give no criterion for which unbalanced starts survive.
     - The collapsed point is still stable, as your own setup says. Survival is still a basin question, but in the (w, p) plane, with the separatrix through the saddle at p₋ as its boundary. The race criterion locates that boundary for p0 ≫ w0.
   - That is the novelty sentence the evidence supports. The "sets aside" wording comes from brief §5.6 (row P1); if you consult `idea-repo`, the same correction applies there.
2. **Weight-decay convention in eq:balance.**
   - "Eq. (6) is the conserved quantity of Tian et al." is right only at α = 1, and the reason is a convention.
   - Tian's Theorem 1, eq. (5), WWᵀ = α_p⁻¹W_pᵀW_p + e^{−2ηt}C, includes weight decay and holds for every α_p, because their predictor decay is −ηW_p. Your flow scales the predictor decay by α, as SGD and AdamW with a per-group learning-rate multiplier do.
   - Say this in one clause, so that the α ≠ 1 remark does not read as a limitation of Tian's result.

**Heads-up for Sec. 4.** The analysis itself belongs to `experiment-repo`; I sent the details in experiment-repo#2.
- **E1's numbers are finite-time ranks.** Per-mode 0.997, exact rank 0.92 and MAE 0.08 are agreement with labels at t = 1500. 98 of the 220 runs whose race had not finished by then, and 25 of the 180 λ = 0 runs, change rank later. Against the final rank, E1's prediction is exact in 0.81 of runs with MAE 0.27. N1 evaluated without the horizon cut predicts the final rank well (exact 0.92, MAE 0.12, in the unfinished runs too).
  - Do not quote E1's numbers as final-rank accuracy.
- **Two rows of the note's heuristic table are contradicted by the model.**
  - The frozen target does collapse under weight decay unless c|w0| > λ.
  - The α row ("rank depends on αλ only") fails in both N1 and E1's measured ranks.
  - Wait for the revised note before writing those rows.

Item 2 (the theory section) stays open.

comments.body:
Your check of `d49f9bb` is addressed at 70cc8ccfa321f7dae9509b58e0639251e487af6c.

**Positioning**
1. **Unbalanced starts in Tian et al.** I removed the "sets aside" sentence and "no basin argument applies".
   - `related.tex` ("Position of this work") now says three things:
     - Tian's per-mode equations and conserved quantity cover unbalanced starts.
     - At η=0 they give a sufficient condition for avoiding collapse.
     - With weight decay, their fixed-point/basin analysis is on the balanced manifold, and which unbalanced starts survive is left open.
   - It then says that survival is still a basin question, in the (a, p) plane, with the separatrix through the saddle at $p_-^k$ as its boundary. For $p_0\gg a_0$ we locate that boundary as a race.
   - Sec. 4.2 opens with the same separatrix sentence.
   - I can't reach `idea-repo` directly, so the brief §5.6 (P1) wording is still uncorrected there. The paper no longer depends on it.
2. **Convention for eq:balance.** `setup.tex` now says it is Tian's Theorem 1 at α=1. Their version holds for every α_p because their predictor decays at rate η. Ours scales that decay by α, as SGD and AdamW with a per-group multiplier do, so for α≠1 the identity holds only at λ=0. The "balanced limit" sentence now refers only to their analysis under weight decay.

**Heads-up items**
- **E1 is reported as rank at T, not final rank.**
  - Sec. 6.1 now says that every E1 agreement figure is agreement with the rank at t=T. In runs with an unfinished race, and in runs at λ=0, the rank can still change after T, so these are not accuracies for the asymptotic rank.
  - The asymptotic rank is left to the held-out runs, which have a convergence check. That is E1b's "converged" definition in experiment-repo 0576788 `results/e1b/prediction.json`.
  - The captions of Figures 2–3 now say "rank at $t=T$" instead of "final rank". The CLAIMS.md C2 status says the same.
  - I have not quoted your final-rank recomputation (0.81 / 0.27). Final-rank numbers will enter only from an experiment-repo results file.
- **Frozen target.**
  - The paper's App. B had the same error as the note ("neither growth nor collapse"). It now gives the Jacobian at (0,0), with det $\alpha(\lambda_W\lambda_P-c_k^2a_0^2)$, and the quasi-static gain equation. The conclusion: under weight decay the frozen target collapses unless $c_k|a_0|>\sqrt{\lambda_W\lambda_P}$, and it regresses onto the random target only at λ=0.
  - T1's row is figtab's. I sent them the correction in figtab-repo#4.
- **α.** App. B claimed the rank depends on α and λ_P "only through their product". That claim is withdrawn: the window and $\lambda_Wt$ in eq. (12) do not scale with α. The Sec. 5 text and T1 only say that α shortens the clock, and they make no product-only claim.

**Build.** I built from the assembled delivery: `make_numbers.py` runs, `latexmk` exits 0, and the PDF has 22 pages with no undefined references and no overfull boxes. The main text still reaches p. 10, as at 96a6d25. The cut to 9 pages will happen together with the held-out results, which also have to fit.

Item 2 stays open. It waits on the revised derivation note and on E1b/E2/E3 (experiment-repo#2).

comments.author: internal-review-repo
comments.body:
**Check of `6152ff5` (Sec. 6.2 E1b), with figtab `0e845f1` and experiment `b802ad6` as assembled now.** This is an early check, not a verdict. My checks are in `internal-review-repo` `checks/`, pushed with this comment.

**Build.** The assembled delivery builds: `make_numbers.py` regenerates `numbers.tex` identical to the committed file, `latexmk` exits 0, the PDF has 23 pages, and there are no undefined references.

**Resolved since my `d49f9bb` check:**
- positioning against Tian (unbalanced starts, separatrix through p_−);
- the α convention of eq:balance;
- E1 reported as rank at t = T;
- frozen target (App. B and the T1 row);
- the "only through the product" claim withdrawn;
- Prop. 2 strict inequality;
- `.pyc` files out of the delivered `code/`.

**Open findings**

1. **Sec. 6.2 claims more than E1b measures: "a run's rank is read at convergence … so E1b tests the asymptotic rank."**
   - Against a long-horizon reduced flow (stable from t = 20000 to 40000), 16 of E1b's 660 aligned runs have a rank at `t_end` that is not final.
   - E1b's convergence rule (rank unchanged over the last fifth) flags all 16 as converged. The rule detects a plateau, and slow directions cross 0.05 after one. `checks/e1b_horizon.json` gives the details.
   - The numbers barely move: against the long-horizon rank, N1 is exact in 0.773–0.782 of the 600 N1 runs with MAE 0.255–0.263, against the reported 0.783 / 0.253 (`checks/e1b_results.json`). The claim does need either experiment-repo's extension of those cells or the wording "rank at the end of training (unchanged over its last fifth)". I raised it in experiment-repo#2.
   - The E1 paragraph at line 19 points to E1b for the asymptotic rank, so it inherits this.
2. **Depth.** Three places attribute the depth error to an unmodelled post-capture stage:
   - Sec. 5, line 18: "depth should act like a larger α as long as the race is decided before capture";
   - Sec. 6.1, line 58 and Sec. 6.2, line 79: "consistent with the (unmodelled) post-capture stage";
   - App. B, line 76: "rank(L,α) ≈ rank(1,Lα); the post-capture stage … not covered".

   The error is in the capture condition itself:
   - With L identity-initialised factors, each weight-decayed, the gain obeys ṗ = αL[p^{2−2/L}(c ā − pσa)a − λ_P p]. Capture therefore needs a² ≥ λ_P p^{2/L−1}/(c − pσ), not a² ≥ λ_P p/(c − pσ).
   - With only that change, scored against E1b's measured labels, the depth error drops:

     | depth | MAE | false survivals |
     |---|---|---|
     | L = 2 | 1.03 → 0.13 | 31 → 0 |
     | L = 3 | 1.40 → 0.33 | 42 → 0 |
     | whole depth arm | 0.81 → 0.16 | 73 → 0 (missed 0 → 14) |

     (`checks/e1b_results.json`, `depth_capture`.)
   - So depth is not "a larger α": with the depth-1 nullcline, N1(L,α) ≡ N1(1,Lα), and that is exactly what over-predicts.

   *What to change:*
   - Report the pre-registered depth failure as measured.
   - Drop the post-capture explanation.
   - Present the corrected capture condition only as a post-hoc derivation, labelled as such, until experiment-repo tests it on held-out data (asked in experiment-repo#2).
3. **Line 121, "to leading order λ_k^race ≈ h_k(p0)/(α log(1/a0))", holds only at α = 1.** In (14), log(λ/c_k) + α^{-1} log(c_k p0/λ) = (1 − α^{-1}) log(λ/c_k) + α^{-1} log p0.
   - The λ-logarithms cancel only at α = 1.
   - For α ≠ 1 they are of the same order as log(1/a0), not subleading.
   - N1's thresholds against the leading-order formula (`checks/e1b_alpha_lam.json`): 0.139 vs 0.434 at α = 0.25 (the leading order even exceeds the static bound there), and 0.048 vs 0.027 at α = 4.
   - At α = 1 the formula works: 0.109 vs N1's 0.088 at a0 = 10⁻², and 0.054 vs 0.049 at a0 = 10⁻⁴. Keeping the dropped O(λ) term (the right side of (14) gains +λ) gives 0.089 vs 0.088.

   *Fix:* state the leading order for α = 1, and keep (14) as an implicit equation otherwise. related.tex line 23 lists "its thresholds" among the new results, so the claim should match.
4. **Line 132: "without a predictor, the net rate is negative for every direction" is stated unconditionally.**
   - App. B (line 60) conditions it on equal marginals, which JEPA masks violate.
   - Under the paper's own eq. (15), c_k > σ_k iff (1−2q)Σ̂_k > 2(1−q)σ̄. At 75 % masking (q = 0.25), every direction with Σ̂_k > 3σ̄ grows without a predictor in the linear model.

   *Fix:* state the condition |c_k| < σ_k + λ_W in both places. The same point went to experiment-repo#2 for Prop. 6 and E2.
5. **Delivered `main.pdf` is stale.** It predates figtab `0e845f1`'s Table 1: page 7 still shows "E1b held-out (pending)" in four rows, while the rebuild shows the E1b entries. Rebuild after each figtab push.
6. **Recorded, expected at this stage:**
   - the main text runs onto p. 10;
   - the abstract, contributions and Sec. 6.3/7 are placeholders;
   - the checklist is TODO;
   - figtab's Fig. 4, Fig. 5 and `tab_e1b` are delivered but not yet included.

   I opened Fig. 4 and Fig. 5: both are readable and labelled, and Fig. 5(a)'s boundary and annotations match `prediction.json` `boundary`.
7. **Fig. 3, for figtab-repo, minor.** I opened it at 300 dpi. Agreement shows as the line passing through the markers, and deviations are visible (e.g. (e) L = 3). Two small fixes:
   - the legend shows the race criterion only as a solid line, but the second series in (b) and (d) is dashed;
   - the grey window and bound lines in (b) and (d) (two dotted, two dash-dot in (b)) are not tied to a series. Label them, or colour them with their series.
8. **Minor:**
   - **Table 2 caption.** It should say "rank at t = T", as the Fig. 2–3 captions now do.
   - **App. A, line 36.** "On {p ≥ p_−} F_k is maximal at p_−" holds only if F_k(p_−) ≥ 0. For p0 > p_+, F_k first falls, and the maximum can be at t = 0.
   - **Def. 4, λ_P = 0 branch with λ_W > 0.** It predicts survival up to T, although Prop. 2(c) rules out a non-collapsed fixed point. Say that this branch is a finite-horizon statement.

The request stays open for E2/E3 and the next revision.

comments.body:
**The E3 results are delivered and verified (experiment `b3077db`), so the E3 write-in can start.** I rescored every criterion independently and regenerated every delivered E3 file from the raw-run release (`internal-review-repo` `ee0d845`, `checks/e3_results.json`, `checks/e3_reanalyze.json`): 0 mismatches. Sources to cite: `results/e3/summary.json`, `summary_followup.json` and `runs.csv`, plus the README "E3 headline".

Two numbers are still being fixed in experiment-repo#2 (comment 163):
- the GPU record: 24 runs used GTX 1080 Ti, not 9;
- Arm T's C-rank split.

Take those two from experiment-repo's next push. Everything below is supported by the delivered files now.

## What the E3 text must carry
1. **Regime and what was tested.**
   - E3 is a transfer test outside the theory's assumptions. Arm T meets SGD, a copied target and decay on every parameter. It does not meet a linear model, a start near collapse, population gradients or co-diagonal statistics. Arm P (AdamW I-JEPA recipe) is further out.
   - The registered predictor is the step-0 horizon rule, the analogue of the growth window, not the race N1. Predictor lr and every target variant get the baseline's prediction.
   - Do not write that the race criterion predicts the ViT rank.
2. **Every registered verdict, failures included.**
   - C-rank: Arm T 0.83 [0.45, 0.99], pass; Arm P 0.12, fail.
   - C-loc: observed 0.0055 against predicted 0.014, a factor of 2.6, fail.
   - C-dir: signed 5/6; nulls 7/20, with all 4 mask settings failing.
   - Theory signs:
     - weight decay passes in both arms;
     - predictor lr fails in both arms (P: 115 → 62 at ×0.1);
     - depth fails (99/115/115);
     - nosg is not complete at epoch 20 (a scale collapse of ×1.5e-4 / ×1.5e-3);
     - frozen target: P passes, T fails;
     - EMA null fails (copy 17, τ 0.9 84, 0.99 117, 0.999 110). That a faster target lowers the rank is post hoc; the slow-EMA sign is untested.
   - C4: theory-prescribed directions 0/3, crossings 0/6.
   - C-full: collapse flags 3/3, probe pass.
3. **What Arm T's pass rests on.**
   - The rule orders the 6 weight-decay configs exactly, and nearly all of the Arm T pass comes from them. It misses predictor init: 115 predicted, 10.3 measured.
   - Every Arm T variant at wd 0.01 ends at 7–11 directions, whatever the target (copy 8.7, frozen 11.0, no stop-gradient 8.3, EMA 7.3) or the predictor (lr ×0.1/×10: 9.3/8.3; init ×0.3/×3: 9.0/10.3). At wd 0 the count is 51.
   - In this arm the dimensional collapse is therefore set by weight decay, not by target feedback or the predictor. Most accounts predict a monotone fall with weight decay. The quantitative test is C-loc, and it fails.
   - The supportable claim: in a ViT, weight decay drives a dimensional collapse whose order the step-0 forces predict and whose location they misplace by a factor of 2.6. E3 does not show the race mechanism, nor the predictor, EMA or masking effects.
4. **Probe.**
   - Both Arm T full-length configs end below the random-init probe of 43.7%: 32.6% and 16.7%.
   - The pass compares two configs that were predicted, and measured, to collapse. It supports "more collapse, lower probe" within Arm T.
   - The only healthy config, F_P_base at 52.3%, uses the other optimiser.
5. **Horizon.** The counts are epoch-20 counts of 50-epoch schedules. At 50 epochs: P_base 115 → 127, T_wd0.01 8.7 → 4.3, T_wd0.03 5 → 4. The collapse flags do not change.
6. **Table 1** needs an E3 entry in the rows E3 tests:
   - weight decay: sign in both arms, transition 2.6× late;
   - predictor lr: fails in both arms;
   - depth: fails;
   - predictor scale: P 1 → 3 fails, T holds in sign only;
   - EMA: registered null fails;
   - mask ratio: the 4 mask settings change the count where the rule predicts no change, and no masking direction was registered;
   - frozen target: currently "not run". Now P keeps its rank and T collapses at wd 0.01, like its baseline;
   - no stop-gradient: incomplete at epoch 20.
7. **Abstract, contribution 3 and Sec. 7.**
   - The E3 sentence needs both the partial pass and the failures.
   - The abstract's "states how predictor scale, learning rate and depth, the target update and the masking ratio enter" needs its linear scope, because E3 contradicts the lr, depth and EMA signs in a ViT.
   - Sec. 7 should list the E3 failures.
8. **App. E3 and checklist item 8.**
   - Architecture, dataset, both arms' hyperparameters, 20 of 50 epochs (3900 steps), 3 seeds, the count definition (eigenvalues ≥ 1e-3 × the largest, 10000 test images), the probe protocol, and the pre-registration commits.
   - Compute from experiment-repo's corrected record (GPU types and run-hours). Item 8 currently names only CPU time.
   - Name neither the cluster nor the release URL; refer to the raw runs as supplementary material.
9. **Figures and tables.** No E3 figure or table is delivered yet. E3's claims need at least the following, from figtab-repo:
   - per-config predicted vs measured count in both arms, with the seed spread, marking the weight-decay sweep against the other knobs;
   - the Arm T weight-decay sweep with the predicted (0.014) and observed (0.0055) transition;
   - the C-full probe against the random-init line.

   Please route this to figtab-repo (paper-repo#8, or a new request).
10. **Page budget.** Page 9 is full, so E3 needs cuts elsewhere. The checker must still PASS.

Approval waits on this write-in and on the two experiment-repo fixes.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) learn representations by predicting the embedding of one part of an input from the embedding of another part, with no negative examples and no reconstruction loss. They are prone to representation collapse, in which the learned embeddings degenerate to a constant or to very low rank. In practice collapse is avoided with a collection of empirical heuristics (how the predictor is designed and scaled, how much of the input is masked, how the target encoder is updated), and no single account explains why they work. The insight to build on: collapse is decided early in training, near the collapsed solution, where two effects compete in every direction of representation space, a driving force that grows the direction and a decay effect that shrinks it. Whether a direction survives, and therefore how much rank the representation can develop, depends on which of the two is stronger there. The research problem is to turn this insight into a theory that explains and predicts when JEPAs collapse and what the common heuristics change, and to test that theory empirically.

Deliver a complete paper that could be submitted to NeurIPS 2026, written to the venue's submission requirements: the LaTeX source in the NeurIPS template, the compiled PDF, and the code and experimental results that the paper's claims rest on.

Do not use any paper, preprint, code release or other written work first published after 1 September 2026.

**What exists.** The A4/N2 theory I pushed (experiment-repo a972088, `theory/ext_A_lntarget.md`) is for **gradient descent**. **Point 4 is done, post hoc, at `70cdda4`. Point 5: E8-X is not run.** Files: `code/checks/e8_regrowth_timing.py` → `results/e8/grid/posthoc/regrowth_timing.json`; text in `results/README.md` (E8 production, after `regrowth_at_switch`). No verdict changes.

**Method**
- The must-regrow segment is ranks 4..39 (T) and 44..127 (P).
- The median segment rank reaching 1e-3 is half the gap regrown. That is exactly B's registered f(20) = 0.5.
- Time is lr-weighted. After e = 10 / 20 there are 40 / 30 lr_max-epochs left in T and 18.4 / 9.3 in P (cosine).
- The growth rate is measured in each hi→lo row itself after its switch: first 5 epochs, first 10, and the rest of the run.

**Results**
- **T: (neither): there is no regrowth to time.** At e = 10 and 20 the segment falls by −0.0085 decades per lr_max-epoch in every window.
  - This equals the slope of one weight matrix decaying under wd_lo = 0.001 with no drive (decoupled decay, −2·lr·wd·spe/ln 10 = −0.0085).
  - That is B-iii's below-separatrix branch (g ≈ −λ_W), not slow regrowth. No horizon recovers it. B's registered premise ("lost directions re-escape under the low threshold") fails in T.
  - Switched at e = 5, the segment rises briefly to −3.30 at epoch 11, then decays.
- **P: (i), regrowth beyond the horizon by its own rate.** The segment regrows at a constant rate in lr-time: 0.09–0.11 decades per lr_max-epoch at e = 10 and 0.14 at e = 20. The flattening after epoch 40 is the cosine lr reaching 0.
  - Reaching f = 0.5 would need 1.2–1.4× (e = 10) and 2.2× (e = 20) the lr-time that is left. The end levels agree: −3.55 and −4.61.
  - Switched at e = 2 / 5, the median segment rank does cross 1e-3, at epochs 13 / 19.
  - So in P, B's mechanism is not contradicted. Its registered f(20) did not account for the horizon.
- **References only.** The constant-lo row's rates on the same ranks bracket everything, so they decide nothing:
  - its fastest 5-epoch rate (warm-up from init) puts every row within the horizon;
  - its mean rate over 50 epochs puts every row beyond it.

**For the claims**
- C6/N5 wording, T: "lost directions keep decaying at the low decay rate; they do not regrow". This is stronger than "not within 30–40 epochs".
- C6/N5 wording, P: "they regrow, but too slowly for the lr left in the cosine schedule (1.2–2.2× short)".
- The asymmetry reading stands in both arms. Its cause differs between them.

**E8-X**
- Not run. Its condition (realised rate > 0 and need/left in (1, 2] for T at e = 10 / 20) is not met: T does not regrow, and a longer T run would only extend the measured decay.
- P meets the timing condition at e = 10 (1.4). But P past epoch 50 runs at lr 0, so testing it would need a longer cosine schedule with new references. That means 4 rows × 5 seeds × 100 epochs, about 15–35 GPU-hours at E8's 0.14–0.32 s per step. It is a new design, and I am not proposing it unless the plan wants P's "beyond the horizon" tested.

issue.body:
**What I need.** A bounded go/no-go from `idea-review-repo` on the E8 production grid (plan v2.5 Sec. 4: "E7/E8 production grids get a bounded go/no-go from idea-review-repo"). idea-review-repo cannot read experiment-repo, so the full registration is given below. Please relay it and bring the decision back here.

**What it is for.** E8 is the ViT decision-time result (claim C6 / new N5 in plan Sec. 5), and its lo→hi rows are B2's warm-up in the ViT. Its outcome sets the plan's exit rule: either the near-collapse premise holds in the ViT, or it is stated as linear-only and B carries the ViT story.

**Registration** (experiment-repo 7029509, `results/e8/prediction.json`, `code/e8_analyze.py`, `code/e8_grid.py`; committed before any production run).

*Frozen code and environment*
- Frozen code: commit fabd62c, `code/vit_jepa.py` md5 e503bee9…, the same file the pilot ran.
- Environment: the delivered E3 cluster venv, torch 2.5.1+cu124. Its 23 packages have the same versions as `results/e3/cluster_env.json`, checked against the pilot's provenance.

*Grid*
- **Arm T:** SGD with momentum 0.9, lr 0.05 constant, copy target, decay on every parameter, no predictor norms. Weight decay low 1e-3, high 3e-2. In E3 these gave epoch-20 counts of 39.3 ± 1.5 and 5.0.
- **Arm P:** the I-JEPA recipe (AdamW, warmup + cosine, EMA 0.996→1, target LN). Its weight-decay ramp is replaced by a constant level before and after the switch; the lr and EMA schedules are unchanged. Weight decay low 0.04, high 5.5. In E3 these gave counts of 115 ± 1.7 and 28 ± 4.6.
- **Rows per arm:** constant low, constant high, low→high and high→low, each switched at e ∈ {2, 5, 10, 20}. The constant rows serve as e = 0 and "never".
- **Size:** 5 seeds, 50 epochs (9750 steps), 20 rows × 5 seeds = 100 runs.

*Statistic*
- The rank measure is the online-token count (eigenvalues ≥ 1e-3 × the largest, on 10000 test images) at epoch 50. Centred RankMe, target count and probe are reported alongside.
- **Equivalence.** A row is equivalent to the never-switched row N iff the Welch 90% CI of the difference in means lies inside ±δ (two one-sided tests at 5%). δ = 0.2·|Δ|, where Δ is the gap between the two constant rows.
- **Informative direction.** A direction counts as informative only if Δ's 95% CI excludes 0 and |Δ| ≥ 5.
- **Decision time D.** D is the earliest e such that every row e' ≥ e is equivalent to N, or ">20".
- **Decision curve.** f(e) = (R(e) − R(N))/Δ, with a bootstrap 95% CI.
- **Sensitivity checks:** margins 0.1 and 0.3; horizons at epochs 30 and 40; D on centred RankMe; D without runs flagged not converged (|R50 − R45| > δ/2).
- **Non-finite runs** are counted and excluded. A row with fewer than 4 finite seeds is "undetermined".

*Prediction*
- From direction B's premise (the post-capture static threshold at the current weight decay; lost directions re-escape; AdamW re-escape per theory note A-ii): D = ">20" and f(20) ≥ 0.5 in all four arm × direction cells. That is, the final rank follows the final weight decay.
- The delivered near-collapse premise predicts D ≤ 5. Both outcomes are reported, and D ∈ {10, 20} is reported at the grid's resolution.
- B's derivation is not written yet; the prediction is qualitative, from its premise.

*Baselines*
- Early reading: the count at epochs 2/5/10/20 vs epoch 50, and at the switch epoch for switched rows.
- The race and the μ count of the constant rows are scored in E7/C5.

*Pilot* (≤ 1 GPU-h, done: SLURM 53929960/53929961, GTX 1080 Ti, 3 runs per GPU, 1 seed, 5 epochs; development only)
- The switch acts at its step. Arm T lo→hi at e = 2 has count 25 at epoch 2 and 19 at epoch 5, against 35 for constant lo and 14 for constant hi.
- Every logged quantity is finite.
- Speed: 0.28-0.34 s/step packed.

*Compute*
- One SLURM array of 34 tasks × 3 runs per GPU, each task ≤ 2 h. A re-run task restarts only the unfinished runs.
- About 50-60 min per task on a 1080 Ti and about 30 min on a V100, so 17-34 GPU-h in total. That is inside the ~90 GPU-h ViT cap; the plan's estimate was 15-18 GPU-h.

**What I already have.** Everything above is pushed, and the driver is ready to submit.

**What waits on this.** Only the E8 production launch. A, B, the E4 development work and the baseline work continue meanwhile.

comments.body:
**Decision: GO** for the E8 production grid as registered at 7029509 (100 runs, 17-34 GPU-h). It comes from `idea-review-repo` (`feasibility.md` v7 at a32c47c, answering idea-review-repo#7). Six conditions are attached. Plan v2.7 (story-repo e0ba464, Sec. 3 C, the bullets after item 6) records them and what they change in the plan.

**Feasibility's basis (measured by them).** `sacct` on Ibex at 2026-10-18 03:10 shows your pilot jobs 53929960/53929961 started 3 min after submission. They took 5.4 and 6.1 min for 5 epochs with 3 runs packed, so about 55-62 min per task at 50 epochs. That matches your registered estimate and is about 2x under the 2 h limit. The `gpu` partition now has 914 jobs pending, so expect longer waits than before. Feasibility could not read your repository, so it took the frozen commit fabd62c and the md5 as stated.

**Conditions (binding for the launch and the analysis):**
1. **Submission.** One tracked array, time limit <= 2 h per task, tasks in priority order:
   - first: the constant rows, and the e = 20 and e = 5 rows of every cell;
   - then: the e = 10 and e = 2 rows.

   Fallback trigger as in v3: no task has started 60 min after submission, or fewer than half have finished 12 h after the first start. **There is no CPU fallback for E8.** A run is 9750 steps, about 27 h at the loaded 10 s/step. If the trigger fires: tell `idea-review-repo` (through me), run the priority subset on whatever starts, label the missing rows, and do not shorten the horizon.
2. **Exit-rule reading.** D = ">20" also arises when row 20 is merely not shown equivalent, for example from under-power at n = 5.
   - Apply "late settings move the rank, premise linear-only" for an arm/direction only when the difference at e = 20 is demonstrated, i.e. the Welch 95% CI of R(20) - R(N) excludes 0.
   - Otherwise report "inconclusive at n = 5". In that case the plan's exit is not triggered.
   - Report both tests, equivalence and difference, for every row.
3. **Non-finite runs.** Keep the registered exclusion. Also report:
   - the count of non-finite runs per row;
   - a sensitivity analysis that scores them as collapsed (rank 0).

   D is "undetermined" if the two scorings disagree.
4. **Provenance per run:** GPU model, torch version, `cluster_env.json` hash, code commit and seed.
5. **Budget.** One re-run of the whole grid is affordable, not several. Do not launch a second E8 grid before the first is analysed.
6. **Reporting.** Arms T and P are reported separately, as registered.

**Notes from feasibility (not conditions):**
- The registration meets their v5 items 1 and 7.
- The qualitative prediction, the same in all four cells, is falsifiable and opposite to the near-collapse premise, which is what the test needs.
- In Arm T high -> low, collapsed runs must regrow from their amplitude at the switch. Report that amplitude beside f(e), so that slow regrowth under SGD is not read as a decided rank. The plan now requires this.

**What this means for your registration.**
- Conditions 2 and 3 add a test (difference at e = 20), a reading ("inconclusive at n = 5") and a second scoring of non-finite runs that `results/e8/prediction.json` and `code/e8_analyze.py` do not yet have.
- They are analysis additions, not changes to the grid or the prediction. Commit them as an addendum to the registration before the production array is submitted, so the record shows they came before any outcome.
- The registration's "late" reading should then cite the demonstrated-difference condition.

issue.body:
**Need:** the plan re-scoped against arXiv 2610.02344. Under the new cutoff (18 Oct 2026) it is prior work, and it is the closest prior work to both the delivered paper and the extension. Please also pass this content to `idea-repo` for a full reading; I cannot reach idea-repo. This comes from internal-review-repo in paper-repo#13. Plan v2.1 Sec. 6 already asks idea-repo for an overlap check. This issue gives what is known so far and what the review will judge.

**The paper (arXiv API, read this turn):**
- **2610.02344v1**, submitted **2026-10-01**: De Melo Costa, Ahn, Popineau, Rimmel and Doan, *Drive vs. Decay: On the Training Dynamics of Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures*. arXiv comment: "Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 (Main Track). 57 pages, 10 pages of main text". Code: github.com/jose-melo/drive-vs-decay.
- **Abstract, verbatim in substance:**
  - It develops "an early-training stability theory that unifies these heuristics". Linearising the coupled JEPA gradient flow around the trivial fixed point gives "a driving force (γ) and a decay effect (σ)".
  - "Under approximate spectral decoupling, a per-mode stability ratio μ_i = γ_i/σ_i factorises into independent data-side and predictor-side terms and the count of unstable modes tracks the rank of representations that can emerge."
  - "The framework predicts a phase boundary, which we confirm empirically across more than 800 Tabular-JEPA configurations."
  - It "unifies predictor scaling, masking ratio, and EMA as distinct mechanisms for shifting μ".
  - It introduces **ResidualPred**, "a transformer predictor whose attention is biased toward the identity at initialisation", which "improves both effective rank and downstream accuracy on tabular benchmarks and in I-JEPA pretraining on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, STL-10, and ImageNet".
- **Less central:** 2609.23881v1 (2026-09-20, MotionJEPA) and 2609.09630v1 (2026-09-09, JEPA Policy) also predate the cutoff now.

**What it means for the plan, as the paper side reads the abstract (idea-repo's reading decides):**
- **Overlaps with the delivered paper's framing.** These are the per-direction drive vs decay at the collapsed point, the count of growing modes as the rank, and the account of predictor, masking and EMA. Novelty claims of contributions 1–3 that rest on that framing must be re-worded.
- **What looks distinct.** Their criterion appears to be *linear instability* at the trivial point: a mode is unstable when μ_i > 1. The delivered paper finds that, with weight decay, the collapsed point is *stable*. There, survival is decided by a transient race between growth and the decaying predictor gain, and the static/instability counts mispredict the rank (E1b: race MAE `\EoneBAlignedMae` against static `\EoneBAlignedBoundMae`; collapse at λ ≈ 0.02–0.09 against the static 0.375). If their μ count is our static bound or initial window, the race is a quantitative advance over it. The extension's A, B and C (Adam/normalised target, post-capture stages, the ladder to the ViT and decision time) look new beyond it. All of this needs the paper itself, not its abstract.
- **What the review will judge** (internal-review-repo `REVIEW_STANDARD.md` E5):
  1. 2610.02344 cited, with what is new relative to it stated precisely.
  2. Wherever both criteria predict the same quantity (rank, collapse boundary, a heuristic's effect), the two compared on the same runs. internal-review-repo is asking experiment-repo for that computation.
  3. If the extension claims a predictor design, a comparison against ResidualPred or a reason why not.
- **For the plan:** the 2610.02344 comparison needs an owner and a slot in E4–E8, ideally on the E1b/E2 held-out runs and on the new held-out grids. If the reading shows a direction of A–C is already done there, A–C need re-scoping.

**What waits on it:** the related-work section, the contribution list, the abstract and the novelty paragraph of the extension. I will write the positioning from idea-repo's reading. Until then I will cite the paper from its abstract only.

comments.author: paper-repo
comments.body:
**For P1 (idea-repo#4): the paper now states that 2610.02344's escape condition with encoder weight decay is the released paper's initial window. Please pass this derivation to idea-repo to confirm or correct. It is at paper-repo 9cd4c88: Sec. 1, Sec. 2, and the appendix paragraph "The stability count of De Melo Costa et al.".**

Derivation, from the v1 PDF, App. J.1 (p48):
- **Their notation.** Their App. J.1 writes γ_kℓ = c_k q_ℓ and σ_kℓ = a_k p_ℓ:
  - a_k and c_k are the eigenvalues of Σ11 and Σ_X1 along data mode k;
  - p_ℓ and q_ℓ are the eigenvalues of P = W_pᵀW_p and Q = W_pᵀM̄_2 along predictor mode ℓ.
- **Encoder decay.** Their Prop. J.1 makes encoder weight decay an additive floor: mode (k, ℓ) escapes iff γ_kℓ − σ_kℓ > η_wd. The decay acts on the context encoder only.
- **Our case.** In the released paper's aligned model, take a scalar predictor gain p0, no target mask (M̄_2 = I) and a stop-gradient or EMA target. Then q = p0, p_ℓ = p0², a_k = σ_k (ours) and c_k = c_k (ours). The condition becomes p0 c_k − p0² σ_k − λ_W > 0, which is g_k(p0) > 0: the initial window.
- **EMA.** Their J.7 says the EMA rate changes the speed of escape, not which modes escape. This matches our result that the EMA root has the sign of g_k at fixed gain.

**What the paper concludes from it:**
- Re-scoring under P2 is mostly done already for E1b aligned. The initial window is the μ count there, and it errs by 3.7 directions against 0.25 for the race. The paper says this in the abstract, contribution 3 and Sec. 2.
- The cases where the identification is **not** immediate are the ones P2 still needs experiment-repo to compute:
  - random Gaussian predictors and non-commuting statistics, where their criterion counts (k, ℓ) pairs under spectral decoupling;
  - masked targets (M̄_2 ≠ I, E2);
  - deep predictors.
- If idea-repo's reading disagrees with the identification, I change the three passages.

The novelty is restated as what their analysis lacks: predictor weight decay (their Lemma 3.4 has a quasi-static predictor and none), collapse as an attractor, the race and λ^race, and the held-out tests. The wording follows your plan v2.3: prior work, framing credited to it. The paper also cites λ-JEPA (2609.35288).

1. **The extension's study plan.** I need its questions, its claims with pre-stated predictions, and which experiments or theory results feed each claim. The plan decides the paper's new sections and its contribution list.

**Input from the paper side.** These are the gaps the delivered paper states itself, from Sec. 7 and Sec. 6 at paper-repo 6e496ca. I offer them as material for the plan, not as a choice of directions:
- **Scope of the theory.** It is a near-collapse analysis of a *linear* model under population gradient flow. It holds only until the first directions reach O(1). It has no noise floor (round-off re-seeds lost directions in three E2 runs) and no post-capture stage.
- **Nonlinear encoders.** Under random masks a tanh encoder gains rank *after* the race, against the near-collapse premise. A two-layer encoder is mispredicted from its initial features.
- **Deep predictors.** The depth correction was made post hoc and re-tested only for identity-initialised factors.
- **Optimiser.** AdamW is at most partly supported. In the ViT the step-0 rule fails under AdamW.
- **EMA.** One pre-registered EMA sign comparison failed. In the ViT the EMA prediction did not transfer.
- **Realistic architecture (E3 ViT).** Only a step-0 rule was tested, not the race. It misplaces the weight-decay transition (factor in `\EthreeLocFactor`). The predictor, EMA and masking predictions failed. In Arm P all four mask settings lowered the rank where no change was registered.
- **Masking.** A predicted fall of rank at high mask ratio held in only some profiles (`\EtwoNonmonoConf` of `\EtwoNonmonoPred`).
- **Heuristic design.** The paper explains the heuristics but derives no design or selection rule from the theory. The objective names this direction.

**Page budget.** The delivered paper fills 9 pages. At the ICLR limit (venue-repo#8 asks for the exact rule), the extension's results need main-text room. I plan to compress the kept material (setup, theory statement, E1/E2) to about 4–4.5 pages and move proofs and the E1 development set to the appendix. That leaves about 4–5 pages for the new results, so a plan with 2–3 new main results fits. More than that would have to go to the appendix.

**Waiting on this:** the new sections, the contribution list and the abstract. I will port the paper to the ICLR template meanwhile, once venue-repo supplies the kit.

issue.author: experiment-repo
issue.body:
**What I need:** the extension plan (plan.md v2) and an updated `assignment.json`. That means picking the research directions for objective experiment-repo#10 and the predictions/experiments I deliver for each. The assignment also still says "NeurIPS 2026 template"; the objective now asks for **ICLR 2027**.

**What it is for:** it decides what goes under `code/`, `results/` and `theory/` for the extended paper. Until then I will not start new runs: no new derivations, predictions or ViT sweeps.

**What the delivered paper leaves open on the analysis side** (my results at 96ecc7d, `results/README.md`; limitations in paper-repo `paper/sections/discussion.tex`):
1. **AdamW, the practice optimizer.** In the ViT, Arm P (AdamW, the I-JEPA recipe) fails the step-0 ranking: Spearman 0.12 (`results/e3/summary.json`, `C-rank arm P`). In the linear model, AdamW is "at most partly supported". The theory assumes plain gradient flow. Adam normalises the tiny near-collapse gradients and decays weights in decoupled form, which plausibly changes the race from exponential growth vs exponential gain decay into roughly linear growth vs decay. This is derivable and can be checked exactly in the linear model on CPU.
2. **Design: weight-decay schedules.** The race says rank is set early, and I-JEPA ramps wd 0.04 -> 0.4. The theory predicts that early wd sets the rank and that a later increase does not remove directions already captured. So a wd warm-up (or separate predictor and encoder decay) should raise rank and probe accuracy at an equal final wd. This is a testable design rule in linear and ViT models.
3. **Post-capture stage, far from collapse.** We observed late rank gains that the near-collapse analysis does not cover: lam=0 linear runs gain directions after t_end, and a tanh encoder under random masks gains rank after the race. A second-stage criterion is possible: once captured directions sustain the predictor, the remaining directions face a static threshold. It would predict which directions are gained late.
4. **Nonlinear encoders.** Two-layer encoders are mispredicted from their initial features. A width/scale sweep (lazy vs rich) would test whether the race holds on the initial features in the lazy regime, and where it breaks. This is CPU-cheap.
5. **The race itself in the ViT.** Only a step-0 rule was tested there, and Arm T's ranking passes only through its wd sweep: post hoc, wd sweep rho 1.0, other factors 0.27. The fix is to log per-direction amplitudes and effective predictor gains over early training and test capture per direction. The force logging already exists (`code/e3_ijepa.py --force-steps`). This can ride on the runs for 1 and 2.

**My recommendation:** 1 + 2 as the core. They explain the main measured failure, and they give a prescription for choosing heuristics that the objective asks for. Add 3 or 4 as the extension beyond near-collapse, with 5 as instrumentation.

**Costs (measured, E3):** 135 ViT runs (8 epochs, a few at 50) took 24.5 run-hours, about 11 min per run. Three seeds share one V100, so a sweep of 30 configs x 3 seeds is about 16 run-hours, or about 6 GPU-hours (`results/e3/compute.json`). Linear and MLP grids run on CPU in local-compute; I will time a pilot before sizing them.

**What I already have:** the linear simulator (`code/linjepa.py`), the exact reduced flow, E1/E1b/E2 grids, the ViT pipeline with both arms, and the SLURM grid driver (`code/e3_grid.py`). All of it is reusable as is.

**How 2610.02344 relates to the delivered paper.** I read the paper and its code. That is exactly the delivered paper's **static initial window**, run by run. So their phase-boundary theory is the step-0/window rule. Our race criterion adds the decay of the predictor, which they do not model. On the delivered held-out runs the race beats their criterion:
- E1b aligned: MAE 0.25 vs 3.74.
- E1b random predictor: 0.69 vs 10.67.
- E2 cyclic masks: 0.03 vs 1.04.

Their criterion wins on the E2 MLP arm (1.90 vs 2.69).

**What this means for the plan:**
- **(a) The race becomes the delivered paper's distinguishing claim.** The paper should be positioned as the race versus their window/μ rule.
- **(b) D2 matters more.** D2 tests the race measured in a ViT. Their image-side μ is also an initialisation-time quantity, and their own appendix calls it "null on images". The race measured during training is the natural extension beyond them.
- **(c) A predictor-design direction (D6) must compare against their ResidualPred.**

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
The previous world in this line of work delivered a complete paper on representation collapse in joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs): a theory in which collapse is decided early in training, near the collapsed solution, by a competition in every direction of representation space between a driving force that grows the direction and a decay effect that shrinks it, together with experiments that test it. That paper, its code and its results are in your repositories and workspaces. Take them as the starting point, not as the work to redo.

Extend that paper with the next piece of research on this problem. Begin from what it leaves open: its stated limitations, its predictions that were not tested or did not hold, the settings its theory does not reach (for example nonlinear or deep encoders, realistic data and architectures, training far from the collapsed solution), and what the theory implies for designing or choosing the heuristics that prevent collapse. Choose the directions that most advance the understanding of when and why JEPAs collapse, and carry them through to new theoretical or empirical results.

Deliver the extended paper, ready to submit to ICLR 2027 and written to the venue's submission requirements: the LaTeX source in the ICLR 2027 template, the compiled PDF, and the code and experimental results that the paper's claims rest on. Keep what still holds from the delivered paper, revise what the new results change, and make clear what the extension adds.

Do not use any paper, preprint, code release or other written work first published after 18 October 2026.

- **Arm T** (SGD with momentum 0.9, constant lr 0.05, copy target, no target LayerNorm, no predictor LayerNorm, decay on all parameters), 13 configs:

**Pre-registration (in progress, does not wait for this):**
- Ibex job 53921685 computes the step-0 force decomposition (drive, self-prediction and decay per eigendirection of the online token covariance) for every run, with no training.
- `code/e3_grid.py predict` turns it into `results/e3/prediction.json`. That file will be committed before any sweep run and will contain:

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) learn representations by predicting the embedding of one part of an input from the embedding of another part, with no negative examples and no reconstruction loss. They are prone to representation collapse, in which the learned embeddings degenerate to a constant or to very low rank. In practice collapse is avoided with a collection of empirical heuristics (how the predictor is designed and scaled, how much of the input is masked, how the target encoder is updated), and no single account explains why they work. The insight to build on: collapse is decided early in training, near the collapsed solution, where two effects compete in every direction of representation space, a driving force that grows the direction and a decay effect that shrinks it. Whether a direction survives, and therefore how much rank the representation can develop, depends on which of the two is stronger there. The research problem is to turn this insight into a theory that explains and predicts when JEPAs collapse and what the common heuristics change, and to test that theory empirically.

Deliver a complete paper that could be submitted to NeurIPS 2026, written to the venue's submission requirements: the LaTeX source in the NeurIPS template, the compiled PDF, and the code and experimental results that the paper's claims rest on.

Do not use any paper, preprint, code release or other written work first published after 1 September 2026.

**Need:** `tools/check_submission.py` (f77da06) should fail the page-limit check whenever any main-text line sits above the References heading on page 10. Today it passes up to 3 such lines.

Computed before training, it predicts the rank and collapse boundary of / held-out linear JEPAs, which the static threshold misses."). The References heading only follows them.
- The checker prints "PASS back matter starts on page 10 after 2 text lines above it on that page; main text must end by page 9" and then "INFO main text length: ends on page 10".

**Suggested change:**
- `spill = pg + 1 == 10 and len(body_before) > 0`, or, if you know of a header line that can legitimately appear there, a tolerance that matches only that line.
- Make the INFO line consistent with the verdict.
- Check it against `11a8c02`'s PDF, which should then FAIL.
